data.title: Abstraction boundaries are optimization boundaries
data.author: delifue
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了N+1查询问题及其由泄漏的抽象导致的原因，通常是由于ORM（对象关系映射）无法自动优化多次查询为单次查询。常见解决方案是降低抽象边界，明确指示ORM批量获取数据。然而，文章提出另一种思路：通过提升抽象边界，将ORM功能集成到语言中，使其能够通过重写规则（如合并N次查询为一次）进行优化。文章还以Haskell的流融合（stream fusion）为例，说明在声明式、纯函数式语言中，提升抽象边界有助于优化。文章总结了一个有趣的模式：提升抽象边界同时提升了优化边界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于编译器优化、ORM（对象关系映射）工具以及抽象边界对优化的影响的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• **[discarded1023]**：认为Haskell等语言能够在模块和抽象边界之间进行优化，提到了Debray在链接时优化的工作以及JVM、MLton等全程序优化编译器的例子。同时指出，经典的数据抽象可以根据使用情况选择或优化实现，提到了2000年代初的相关研究。

• **[mrkeen]**：指出ORM存在“泄漏抽象”问题，导致无法自动优化查询，例如N+1问题。同时提到Haskell和SQL是声明式/纯函数式的，因此更易于优化，而ORM则不是。他还提到了Haxl作为解决方案。

• **[joshdata]**：质疑是否存在编译器解决方案来防止坏查询。建议通过明确标记函数类型或避免在循环中使用数据库连接来改善问题，强调了对数据库连接的显式管理。

• **[cogman10]**：认为编译器无法进行期望的优化，因为编译器不理解SQL和数据的存储方式，也无法感知数据集的当前状态。他指出，RDBMS通过大量统计数据进行优化，而编译器难以复制这种性能。

• **[wavemode]**：同意抽象边界是优化边界，但认为不需要将ORM查询变成语言的一部分来提高边界。以Django ORM为例，指出通过返回QuerySet等技术，可以让调用者有更多控制和优化机会。

• **[vjerancrnjak]**：主张避免使用ORM，认为其设计目标是封装而不是效率。建议使用更高效的方法预加载上下文，而不是依赖ORM的懒加载特性。

• **[nyrikki]**：认为ORM不是一个好的抽象例子，因为SQL的声明式模型与命令式编程存在阻抗不匹配。讨论了SQL隐藏复杂性以及不同持久化模型的权衡分析。

补充讨论：
• **Haxl作为N+1问题的解决方案**：[mrkeen]提到了Haxl作为解决N+1问题的实际案例，提供了一种优化的可能性。
• **全程序优化和编译器优化边界**：[discarded1023]提到了全程序优化编译器（如MLton）以及早期研究，表明编译器在某些情况下可以跨越抽象边界进行优化。
• **ORM设计的权衡**：[nyrikki]和[vjerancrnjak]都提到了ORM的设计初衷是封装和易用性，而非效率，因此在效率问题上可能需要考虑其他方案。

争议焦点：
• ORM的效率和设计权衡：一部分评论者（如[vjerancrnjak]和[nyrikki]）认为ORM的设计初衷和效率之间存在矛盾，主张避免使用ORM。
• 编译器优化的可行性：[cogman10]和[joshdata]对编译器能否解决坏查询问题持怀疑态度，而[discarded1023]和[wavemode]则认为在某些情况下编译器或语言特性可以帮助优化。

总结：讨论围绕ORM的效率问题、编译器优化的可行性以及不同编程语言和工具在处理数据库查询优化时的表现展开。争议的核心在于ORM的设计是否适合高效查询，以及编译器能否有效解决查询优化问题。

44404831.article_content:
Abstraction boundaries are optimization boundaries
The N+1 query problem occurs when your application code sends one SQL query per element in a collection. The N queries are redundant; since all of the data is in the database already, a single query should be enough.
This problem is usually caused by a leaky abstraction; the ORM, or whatever database abstraction you are using, can’t anticipate that it would need to send N queries, so it can’t automatically optimize this down to a single query. The solution is usually to move the abstraction boundary
down
, and explicitly tell the ORM that you will need to fetch a set of rows in bulk, rather than repeatedly fetching single rows.
But what if we could do it the other way around? Can we solve the problem by moving the abstraction boundary
up
instead?
The problem with the ORM example is that the compiler doesn’t know what the ORM does, and as such it can’t optimize it; to the compiler it’s just another piece of userland code. However, what if we raise the abstraction boundary and make the ORM part of the language? This means that we could formulate rewrite rules for the ORM, allowing it to eg merge the N queries into a single query.
There are other examples of this: Haskell has support for adding rewrite rule pragmas to libraries; among other things this is used to optimize list operations using
stream fusion
. However, this only works since Haskell is declarative / pure; the low-level operational semantics (like evaluation order) are abstracted away from the programmer, and as such are amenable to optimization.
I think there’s an interesting pattern here: By raising the abstraction boundary we have also raised the optimization boundary.

data.title: Show HN: I built the tool I wished existed for moving Stripe between countries
data.author: felphos
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stripe账户迁移服务的可行性、定价、技术与法律问题以及隐私和数据保护

不同观点：
• egorfine建议提高价格，因为该服务是一次性交易，且对有需求的客户至关重要，他还提出按客户数量定价的建议。
• x13关注商标和标志的使用问题，担心在服务中使用Stripe的标志可能会引发法律问题。
• janmo分享了自己两年前类似的经历，指出Stripe在迁移和B2B功能上的不足，如缺乏公司名称字段和发票更正功能。
• e28eta作为Stripe的前员工，指出潜在的问题包括账户接管和Stripe API版本变更的长期管理。
• mtmail提到他们五年前的经历，Stripe的客户服务帮助复制了客户数据，但订阅需要手动处理。
• matthewtse分享了自己进行跨国账户迁移的艰难经历，并建议将服务目标定位为B2B工具，同时建立声誉。
• citizenpaul认为这种迁移服务可能是一个小众市场，服务商需要高收费才能盈利，并建议改变定价模型。
• absoluteunit1对跨国切换的复杂性表示关注，并表示未来可能会用到相关服务。
• kundi担心隐私和数据保护问题，强调处理Stripe账户时需要高度的谨慎和数据保护。
• xyst认为Stripe应该原生支持这种迁移功能，并希望被收购以实现此功能。
• Horffupolde质疑Stripe是否允许这种迁移服务。
• elemeno指出网站上的语法错误，建议将"transfers everything seamless"改为"seamlessly"。
• pxue质疑为什么选择这种方法而不是使用记录商户。
• joshstrange建议更改服务名称，因为包含“Stripe”可能会引发麻烦。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是服务名称中包含“Stripe”是否会引发法律问题，部分评论者如x13和joshstrange对此表示担忧。
• 另一个讨论点是服务的定价策略，egorfine和citizenpaul提出了不同的定价建议，包括按客户数量定价和针对B2B市场的定价策略。
• 技术问题如API版本变更和数据迁移的具体操作也被多次提及，e28eta和mtmail分享了他们的经验和见解。
• 隐私和数据保护也是一个重要的讨论点，kundi强调了处理Stripe账户时需要高度的谨慎和数据保护措施。

data.title: Show HN: Jobs by Referral: Find jobs in your LinkedIn network
data.author: nicksergeant
data.article_summary:
JobsByReferral.com帮助用户通过LinkedIn网络寻找工作机会。它通过分析用户下载的LinkedIn数据，找到用户 connections 所在公司的职位空缺，从而增加被推荐和获得面试的机会。具体步骤包括：

1. 下载LinkedIn数据档案（通过“数据隐私”设置获取完整数据，包括Connections.csv文件）。
2. 可选择使用demo数据体验功能。
3. 上传LinkedIn数据文件（ZIP格式或Connections.csv文件）开始搜索。

该工具旨在利用已有的人脉网络，提高求职成功率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LinkedIn网络内搜索功能及其相关问题

不同观点：
• Gergely和Floutist44认为LinkedIn已经存在"在你的网络中"的搜索过滤功能，且该功能已使用多年，新的AI搜索只是让这个功能更加智能化。
• Hackernewds对该功能表示赞赏，认为这是LinkedIn早就应该开发的功能。
• 1970-01-01指出，有些人虽然保留LinkedIn档案，但并不活跃，因此该功能可能不完全有效。
• Thih9关注个人数据隐私问题，询问数据是否被存储或用于其他目的，是否有隐私政策保护用户数据。
• B8提到在其他平台如Blind上可以获得推荐，但质疑LinkedIn上随机添加的人是否会真正提供推荐。
• Fuzzy1000建议增加一个功能，可以精确定位和分析人际网络中的连接。
• Orliesaurus将这个功能比作Blind的升级版。
• Dijit提出相反的需求，希望有一个推荐之前共事过的优秀同事给当前公司的功能，并描述了自己曾经尝试开发该功能的经历。
• Shados认为这个功能展示了AI将如何彻底改变行业，并讨论了LinkedIn内部可能的产品开发流程，强调外部开发者能更快实现新功能。
• Bsoles关注数据安全问题，引用LinkedIn要求用户下载和提供整个LinkedIn数据的做法，提出担忧。
• Toyg对功能实现方式提出质疑，认为这是在让用户进行LinkedIn数据抓取，建议使用官方API，并指出该服务在GDPR合规性上的重大影响。

补充讨论：
• 数据隐私和合规性是讨论中的一个重要问题，特别是对于欧洲用户的GDPR合规性。
• 功能的实现方式引起了一些争议，特别是关于使用官方API和用户数据抓取的问题。
• 对功能的实际效果和用户使用习惯存在不同看法，例如对不活跃用户档案的过滤效果和推荐的真实性。

• 数据隐私和合规性是讨论中的一个重要问题，特别是对于欧洲用户的GDPR合规性。
• 功能的实现方式引起了一些争议，特别是关于使用官方API和用户数据抓取的问题。
• 对功能的实际效果和用户使用习惯存在不同看法，例如对不活跃用户档案的过滤效果和推荐的真实性。

data.title: Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna – Nuclear propulsion and solar sailing
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了利用先进推进技术前往太阳系边缘天体塞德娜的可行性。研究评估了两种推进方案：基于D-³He热核聚变的直接融合驱动（DFD）火箭引擎，以及利用涂层热脱附进行推进的太阳帆。对于DFD方案，分析假设了一个1.6兆瓦的系统，能够实现约10年抵达塞德娜，其中包括1.5年的持续推力。而对于太阳帆，则考虑通过木星引力辅助进行飞越，预计7年完成任务。研究还考虑了有效载荷能力、旅行时间、科学回报以及通信限制等关键参数。结果为未来深空探测任务规划提供了基础对比。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sedna探测任务的可行性及相关推进技术（尤其是直接融合驱动技术）的发展现状和前景

不同观点：
• **pavel_lishin** 对Direct Fusion Drive（DFD）的实际进展表示怀疑，特别是其可靠性和能否在太空长时间运行。同时指出，鉴于Sedna的轨道特性，传统推进系统需要长达30年的深空旅行，因此任务需要尽快启动。
• **myrmidon** 认为DFD是一个有趣的概念，可能为未来的星际旅行提供可能性，但对DFD如何选择D/He3融合而不是D/D融合表示困惑，并担心中子辐射问题。
• **mikewarot** 提到了过去的核裂变项目（如Project Rover），认为近期的核系统可能更可行，并指出在轨的OTP-2卫星已经使用了创新的推进系统，包括“融合增强”的离子推进器。
• **stevenAthompson** 提出了一种替代方案，建议发射大量小型网状探测器，利用数量优势和低成本（类似手机成本）来弥补单个探测器的性能不足。
• **pier25** 认为即使使用DFD，到达Sedna也需要长达40年的时间线，质疑是否有组织能够长期维持这样的项目预算和规划。
• **jmyeet** 对所有提到的推进技术持怀疑态度，认为目前的技术都处于非常初期的阶段，尚未经过实际验证，特别是核推进技术。此外，对长时间任务中探测器的生存能力和太阳帆的耐久性表示担忧，并建议将资源投入到天王星或海王星的探测任务中。

补充讨论：
• **accrual** 认为Sedna的远距离探测可能揭示其表面分子的意外信息，有助于理解其起源和远处的太空环境。
• **ananddtyagi** 以《三体》小说作类比，暗示任务的复杂性和科幻性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于当前推进技术（尤其是DFD）的实际可行性和成熟度，以及长时间深空任务中探测器的生存能力与任务规划的现实性。

Title:
Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts
Authors:
Elena Ancona
,
Roman Ya. Kezerashvili
,
Savino Longo
View a PDF of the paper titled Feasibility study of a mission to Sedna -- Nuclear propulsion and advanced solar sailing concepts, by Elena Ancona and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Exploring the outer reaches of the Solar System presents significant propulsion and mission design challenges. This study assesses the feasibility of a mission to Sedna using two advanced propulsion concepts: the Direct Fusion Drive (DFD) rocket engine, based on D-$^{3}$He thermonuclear fusion, and a solar sail utilizing thermal desorption of its coating for propulsion. Both are evaluated for a one-way Earth-to-Sedna mission; however, due to the different performances the DFD would enable orbit insertion, whereas for the solar sail a flyby is envisioned. The analysis evaluates key mission parameters, including delivered payload capacity, travel time, and potential science return. For the DFD, we assume a 1.6 MW system with constant thrust and specific impulse, while for the solar sail, we consider acceleration via thermal desorption and a gravity-assist maneuver around Jupiter. The mission analysis incorporates four key phases: departure, interplanetary acceleration, interplanetary coasting, and rendezvous. Sedna is expected to pass through the perihelion of its orbit in 2075--2076 and then move again away from the Sun. Considering the distances involved, a mission targeting the object would need to be launched "relatively" soon, especially if using conventional propulsion systems, which could require up to 30 years of deep-space travel. In our study, results indicate that the DFD could reach Sedna in approximately 10 years, with 1.5 years of thrusting, while the solar sail, assisted by Jupiter's gravity, could complete the journey in 7 years. The feasibility of science payload accommodation, power availability, and communication constraints is also considered. These findings provide a comparative foundation for future deep-space mission planning.

data.title: Aesop in Words of One Syllable
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 《Aesop in Words of One Syllable》是一本独特的儿童读物，出版于19世纪，属于玛丽·戈多芬（Mary Godolphin）创作的“单音节”系列。该书用简单的单音节词汇重写了伊索寓言，旨在让孩子们更容易阅读。玛丽·戈多芬本名露西·艾金（Lucy Aikin），是英国著名的历史学家、诗人和女性主义者，对儿童教育有浓厚兴趣。这本书包含99个寓言故事，如《狼来了》和《狐狸与葡萄》，但像《龟兔赛跑》等故事因无法用单音节词表达而未收录。该书通过Distributed Proofreaders和Project Gutenberg等志愿者项目得以保存和传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用单音节词语的词典及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [alnwlsn] 介绍了一个包含约2500个单音节词的词典，并提供了几个例子。该用户认为这种词典很有趣且独特，但并未深入讨论其有效性或应用场景。
   
• [pinko] 认为该词典的作者在某些地方作弊，例如使用连字符将多音节词（如"butch-ers"）分割成单音节，质疑其纯粹性。

• [teraflop] 猜测该词典可能启发了Guy Steele的"Growing a Language"演讲，或两者独立得出了相似的概念，提供了相关视频链接。

• [gweinberg] 质疑坚持使用单音节词的必要性，认为使用常见词即可，并指出人们最早学习的词汇通常是双音节的，如重复的音节。

• [esafak] 支持使用简化语言的想法，并分享了自己与孩子阅读维多利亚时代翻译版本的困难，认为现代儿童可能难以理解复杂的语言结构，提供了具体例子。

• [cckolon] 提到Randall Monroe对简单英语的痴迷，通过链接引用xkcd漫画，暗示单音节词语的应用在其他领域也有体现。

• [josefritzishere] 提供了背景信息，指出该类书籍有一个系列，并提到某些书籍通过连字符化来满足单音节标准，提供了相关历史出版信息和链接。

• [JKCalhoun] 更喜欢在Archive.org而非Project Gutenberg上查看该类书籍，并个人对每篇故事末尾的道德总结表示不喜欢。

• [vintermann] 分享了自己用单音节词做游戏的经历，但认为这种方法作为儿童教育工具不太实用，因为一旦不小心使用了多音节词，就可能导致困惑，且认为这不是必须遵循的规则。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于单音节词词典的纯粹性和实用性。部分用户质疑作者是否严格遵循了单音节规则，以及这种方法在实际教育中的有效性。

• 不同用户对简化语言的看法各异，有的认为有助于儿童理解，有的则认为现代儿童难以理解复杂的古代语言结构。

• 用户们还分享了相关资源和背景信息，丰富了讨论的深度和广度。

44433843.article_content:
Hot off the Press
Book Reviews and News from Distributed Proofreaders
Home
About
Aesop in Words of One Syllable
In the 19th Century, British and American children’s literature evolved from puritanical moral and religious instruction to delightfully imaginative tales meant to awaken a sense of wonder. But morality and imagination could certainly thrive together.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is an excellent example of this.
The ancient Greek storyteller
Aesop
may or may not have existed, and he may or may not have written the hundreds of morality tales attributed to him. Yet his stories have been popular from the time of Aristotle to the present day, and their morals have contributed classic expressions like “sour grapes” to the English language. The first English version, printed by William Caxton in 1484, was intended for adults. In the 16th and 17th Centuries, English schoolboys were taught Latin and English from various translations of the fables. It wasn’t until the 18th Century that the fables began to appear in illustrated editions intended to entertain (while edifying) children. And in the 19th Century, with the flowering of children’s literature, there was a veritable explosion of illustrated Aesops.
Æsop’s Fables in Words of One Syllable
is unique among the illustrated editions: It’s written entirely in words of one syllable (except for the title, of course). It’s part of a “One Syllable” series written between 1867 and 1870 by Mary Godolphin, the pen name of
Lucy Aikin
. Aikin was a prominent English historian, poet, and feminist who also took a keen interest in the education of children. Other books in her “One Syllable” series include
Robinson Crusoe
,
The Swiss Family Robinson
, and
The Pilgrim’s Progress
. They’re all designed to make reading them easy for children.
The Aesop volume, in an 1895 edition published after Aikin’s death, contains 99 fables, including those featuring the boy who cried wolf, the fox and the grapes, and the goose that laid the golden (“gold”) egg. Notably absent are “The Tortoise and the Hare” and “The Ant and the Grasshopper,” perhaps because Aikin couldn’t come up with one-syllable synonyms for some of those creatures. But there’s plenty here to enjoy, thanks to the volunteers at Distributed Proofreaders and Project Gutenberg.
This post was contributed by Linda Cantoni, a Distributed Proofreaders volunteer.

• 不同用户对简化语言的看法各异，有的认为有助于儿童理解，有的则认为现代儿童难以理解复杂的古代语言结构。

data.author: hnand
data.article_summary: HackerNewt是一款第三方Hacker News客户端，通过独特的评论树展示方式，解决传统界面评论过窄和层级不清的问题。其优点包括：评论宽度保持不变、始终显示当前评论的父评论、通过滑动控制子树浏览，以及轻松跳过不感兴趣的子树。此外，应用还提供自定义板块、搜索、阅读列表等功能，提升阅读体验。不过，部分用户反馈应用曾出现加载问题，但开发者迅速修复。该应用不隶属于Hacker News官网，隐私保护良好，免费下载但包含内购。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Hacker News的第三方应用及其功能改进建议

不同观点：
• goodburb建议添加一个持久保存的过滤功能，用于过滤特定话题（如政治或AI），并提到目前使用的替代工具。
• pvg引用了2年前的一个相关讨论，暗示该问题或类似功能建议早已存在。

• krishnasangeeth提到自己曾开发过类似应用，并分享了其应用链接，指出其应用风格与官网相似，且包含一些独特的交互设计。
• afro88对应用的发布表示赞赏，解决了其在HN使用中遇到的问题（如评论折叠不便），但也提到遇到了列表项重复的bug。
• thebruce87m将该应用与HACK进行比较，表达了对HACK长期存在崩溃问题的失望，暗示可能考虑切换应用。
• vrighter对应用的创新性提出质疑，认为其设计类似于默认折叠的树状视图，要求进一步解释差异。
• xp84表示已经使用了该应用的早期版本，并对替代方案的出现表示欢迎，感谢社区开发者的贡献。

• sneak对应用不监控用户数据表示感谢，并提到已购买高级版本以支持开发者。
• fraXis询问是否会发布Android版本，显示了对跨平台支持的关注。

• ashish01提到自己实现了BFS扩展评论的功能，并分享了一个支持暗黑模式的网页应用链接。

data.title: Graph Theory Applications in Video Games
data.author: haywirez
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了Clara Nguyễn关于图论在电子游戏中应用的演讲内容。演讲涵盖了图论的基本概念及其在游戏开发中的实际应用，包括：3D图形的顶点和边如何在图形中表示和处理，赛车游戏中的圈数计算，利用并查集生成迷宫，以及bitDP理论的应用等。演讲还讨论了1982年Atari 2600游戏《Entombed》中的一个未解问题。演讲时长为60-75分钟，内容深入，并包含与听众的互动。文章还提供了几个技术性问题及其答案，以帮助听众理解演讲内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用及其具体实现方法

不同观点：
• [j2kun] 认为Graph Theory在视频游戏中的应用不仅仅限于理论，有许多实际应用，例如在视频游戏中的路径寻找等。然而，他指出文章中提到的某些应用似乎更偏向于假设性，缺乏实际使用证据。虽然作者没有提供这些技术在游戏设计中被实际应用的证明，但[j2kun]仍然肯定了作者提出这些想法的贡献，只是认为标题和引言具有误导性。

• [Llamamoe] 指出文章遗漏了图形语法（graph grammar）在关卡生成中的应用，特别是由游戏Unexplored首创的关卡生成算法。他认为这是一种非常吸引人的程序化生成（procgen）算法，值得讨论。

• [palmfacehn] 强调了在大型房间和走廊网络中寻找路径的明显应用，认为这是Graph Theory在游戏中的一个直接而实用的例子。

• [tantalor] 对文章未提及平面性（planarity）表示失望，暗示平面性作为Graph Theory的一个概念，在视频游戏中可能具有潜在的应用价值。

补充讨论：
• 文章标题和内容的匹配度是[j2kun]提出的一个争议点，他认为标题和引言可能误导读者以为所有提到的应用都是已被实际使用的技术。
• [Llamamoe]补充了图形语法关卡生成的具体实例，增加了对实际应用案例的讨论。
• [palmfacehn]通过具体场景（大型房间和走廊网络中的路径寻找）进一步论证了Graph Theory的实际应用。
• [tantalor]提出了对平面性的关注，虽然没有详细展开，但提示了这一概念在游戏设计中的潜在应用。

总体来看，讨论围绕Graph Theory在视频游戏中的实际应用和假设应用展开，参与者提供了不同的具体应用实例和概念，并对文章内容的全面性提出了看法。

Description:
A detailed look at Graph Theory and how it can be applied to video games.
Slogan:
There's more to this than you think...

Talk Summary & Table of Contents
Graph Theory isn't just a topic that is restricted to being
"theory". There are several real-life applications of it. One of
those just happens to be video games. In this talk, I go over a
brief overview of several concepts where Graph Theory is applied.
The topics covered vary a bit:
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
-
Vertices in 3D space, how they are represented, and the
"rules" of dealing with vertices and edges.
Race Games & Lap Counting
-
Racing games where circuits are used to count laps, as
well as a mention of
Mario Kart Wii
and its Ultra-Shortcuts, to encourage
the simplicity of Hamiltonian Circuit checking for lap
counting.
Maze Generation w/ Disjoint-Sets & Union-Find
-
I talk about how to generate mazes efficiently, as well as
taking it a step up. Generation of multiple connected mazes
along with multi-floor/dimensional mazes are described. The
true power of the Disjoint-Set data structure with
optimisations is also discussed in depth.
bitDP, a theoretical approach
-
As a bonus, a theoretical "Part 2" to
my bitDP talk
is
included too. I talk about the theory behind it and how it
can be applied to a game to optimally guarantee that a
Hamiltonian Path exists in a generated graph.
Entombed (1982 Atari 2600 game)
-
For an added bonus, I also discuss an unsolved problem
involving an Atari 2600 game,
Entombed
.
Just a heads up, this talk is
60-75 minutes long
. Concepts
will be discussed in great depth. However, the talk was
intentionally constructed for me to be over-prepared, with topics
that can be skipped if I do not have time to cover everything. As
such, I link to this page in the slides if anyone is interested in
the full talk. Audience interaction is welcome mid-talk. In the
event that I skip topics, the questions below are guaranteed to be
covered while I'm talking.
Questions
As a requirement, we had to put questions in for the audience to
answer on paper mid-talk. The answers were hidden in the slides to
see if students were paying attention. Here are mine, with answers
at the end of the page:

M
of
n
vertices, how many triangles are drawn if done via
Triangle List
?

*

65536
)? Alternatively, what is the lg
*

2)?
What does bitDP stand for?
The "rules" of graphs in graphics
Most graphs discussed in our Graph Theory are abstract and may be
visualised in any way as long as it follows a set of rules.
Likewise, in computer graphics, there are "rules" too. However,
they are quite different from the theoretical graph theory we are
used to discussing. How a vertex and an edge are percived are
different and absolute.
Here's a few rules:
Vertices have
positional
coordinates (x, y, z) to
define position in space. Consequently, this means that
there is only
one
way to represent them in space.
Edges (connections between vertices) are
implied
,
based on a drawing mode of the programmer's choice. They
all have their own advantages and disadvantages. I'll
go over them below.
Everything is oriented around
triangles
. Period. If
you wanted to make a square, you do it with two triangles.
If you wanted to make a curved surface, you have to
estimate it with triangles.
Coordinate Systems
We have three dimensions to work with here. The coordinates are
cartesian, and denoted with (x, y, z). Depending on implementation,
you may find the "y" axis being the "height" axis, or the "z" axis
being the "height" axis. For simplicity of this talk, any potential
discussion of 3D coordinates will assume "z" as the "height" axis.
This is shown as follows:
Z-axis being shown as the "height" axis.
Back-Face Culling
When we draw a triangle, it's filled, obviously. However, only one
side of the triangle is drawn. The other side is invisible. This is
due to
Back-Face Culling
. The side that gets drawn depends
on the order the vertices are facing when you draw to the screen.

data.title: All Good Editors Are Pirates: In Memory of Lewis H. Lapham
data.author: Caiero
data.article_summary: 这篇文章纪念了美国散文家兼编辑刘易斯·H·拉普姆（Lewis H. Lapham），他于2024年7月23日去世。作者聚焦于与刘易斯共事的时光，特别是拉普姆季刊（Lapham’s Quarterly）的创立过程。2007年，刘易斯在纽约曼哈顿创办该杂志，办公室里充满了书籍和知识的气息。作者作为首位全职编辑加入，见证了杂志从无到有，逐渐发展到拥有四万订阅者和年度盛会的过程。刘易斯工作勤奋，每期杂志的开篇文章都精心打磨，多次修改。他平易近人，乐于听取每个人的意见，尽管他出身名门，却常讽刺美国统治阶级。作者回忆起与刘易斯共度的时光，包括在酒吧讨论杂志内容和设计的夜晚，对他充满敬佩与怀念。

• [svara] 对Lapham的播客《The World in Time》给予高度评价，认为Lapham像是来自另一个时代的人物，强调其独特性。
• [PostOnce] 被文章顶部的图片吸引，引发对舞台设计模型和微缩模型的研究兴趣，偏离了原本对Lapham的讨论。
• [ggm] 提到Robertson Davies和E. Anne Proulx曾用小镇报纸编辑为主题进行写作，可能暗示Lapham的编辑风格与这些作家的文学主题有相似之处。
• [Aachen] 引用了文章中的一句话，指出Lapham认为“所有优秀的编辑都是海盗”，他们从每个人那里偷取灵感，以此解释编辑的创造性过程。

This remembrance first appeared in
Stranger’s Guide
on July 28, 2024.
O
n July 23, 2024, the American essayist and editor Lewis H. Lapham died. Since then several beautiful obituaries have been written about the great man and I won’t attempt to repeat these, though I certainly encourage reading them. Instead I want to focus on a very particular time and place where I worked with Lewis and knew him best—the book-filled offices of his last great project,
Lapham’s Quarterly
.
After a storied tenure of nearly thirty years at
Harper’s Magazine
, Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
in 2007 as a magazine of the history of ideas. The offices were housed on Irving Place just off Union Square in Manhattan. Here I spent eight years as executive editor and found the offices to be a magical place filled with knowledge, wit, history, literature, and cigarette smoke. In those book-lined rooms I got an up-close lesson on how to start a magazine and how to run it with grace. It’s also where I met Abby Rapoport,
Stranger’s Guide
’s publisher and my co-founder as we built our own magazine years later.
Back in 2007 I was the first full-time editorial hire Lewis made. On my first day of work, I was greeted by the only other staff members in the office. The first was Ann Gollin, Lewis’ rock and longtime assistant. The second was a young intern in flip-flops and cut-off shorts. That was it, that was the entire operation. There was no website, no magazine, no subscribers. Instead there was just the beginning of Lewis’ idea that we cull through the great books and create a digest of thought and ideas. Each issue would be on a new theme, be it war, religion, or food.
When I left eight years later, Lewis had built a thriving magazine with forty thousand subscribers and an annual gala—the Decades Ball—headlined by the likes of Tom Hanks and Anne Hathaway. There was a robust intellectual editorial board that met four times a year around a large wooden table to discuss
Thucydides
,
Marx
, or
Hannah Arendt
.
But that all came later. On that very first day of work, Lewis took me out, first to a party at André Schiffrin’s penthouse apartment, where he introduced me to
Joan Didion
before slipping out to a late dinner at Elaine’s. Here we sat at what Lewis assured me was the best table in the house. Within minutes the grande dame herself, Elaine, plopped down at our table with a tremendous sigh, as if we were just the port in the storm she’d been waiting for. An endless stream of people dropped by to say hello or to drink or to argue politics late into the night. I was accustomed to a very different crowd—those of small leftist magazines and the New School philosophy graduate students.
“Where am I?” I wondered. “What have I just signed on to?”
When Lewis founded
Lapham’s Quarterly
, he had already been inducted into the American Society of Magazine Editors Hall of Fame. He was already famous as an essayist, editor, and author of countless books. But despite all his accolades, those early days at
Lapham’s Quarterly
had the feel of a 1940s movie about a plucky team of actors putting on a show, a kind of “Gee shucks folks, let’s make a magazine!” On Lewis’ desk, next to the ashtrays and the blue folders full of notes, sat the book
How to Start a Magazine
, which was hurriedly tucked away the day the
New York Times
came to photograph the offices. In those days, I was married to the magazine’s art director and we didn’t yet have kids. So almost every evening after work we’d head off for drinks with Lewis at the nearby bar, Paul & Jimmy’s, where Lewis quickly established himself as a regular. It was here we spent countless hours discussing this nascent publication, its cover, the printer, the feel of an issue, and ideas for themes and authors.
Lewis was an incessantly hard worker; he was the first to arrive at the office and the last to leave. Almost every night after work he’d head off to a dinner, a book party, or some other glamorous literary event. Although he was already in his seventies, I never saw a man work harder.
Each issue of
Lapham’s Quarterly
opened with an essay by Lewis that he would painstakingly labor over for weeks; seventeen drafts for one essay was not uncommon. Ann Gollin, his trusty accomplice in all things great and small, would diligently transcribe the essays he dictated on a small hand-held tape recorder. And then she’d transcribe them again, then yet again, as he crafted and re-crafted each sentence.
Lewis would show everyone in the office his drafts, from the interns to the publisher, asking eagerly, “What do you think?” He looked for ideas and input everywhere. He was never an elitist even though he summered in Newport, his pocket squares were crisp, and his cufflinks shined. Lewis’ essays poked fun at the American ruling class from his position within the belly of the beast.

data.article_summary: 2025年7月1日，PlanetScale宣布推出私密预览版**PlanetScale for Postgres**，号称是全球最快的Postgres托管平台。该平台响应客户需求，旨在解决当前Postgres托管平台常见的宕机、性能差和成本高的问题。PlanetScale for Postgres使用真实Postgres运行于其专有操作器上，提供高可用性、自动故障转移、查询缓冲和连接池等功能，并支持无停机自动更新Postgres版本。此外，PlanetScale Metal的本地NVMe SSD驱动器显著改善了云中托管关系数据库的性能/成本比。虽然Vitess是PlanetScale的强项，但为了适应Postgres，正在从头构建新系统，未来将提供更多信息和早期访问机会。公司邀请运行大规模Postgres的企业参与合作。感兴趣者可注册私密预览等候名单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PlanetScale 推出 PostgreSQL 服务的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• joshstrange：他从 PlanetScale 转向了 Neon，因为 PlanetScale 不支持每个租户一个数据库，而且需要为每个数据库支付高额费用。他的使用场景是小规模、自筹资金的公司，负载波动大但可预测。他认为 Neon 更适合他的需求，但仍然对 PlanetScale 抱有期待，并赞赏其产品和支持服务。

• kellysutton：作为一名使用 PlanetScale MySQL 两年的用户，他认为这是 PostgreSQL 社区的一个令人兴奋的消息。他将使用 PlanetScale 的体验比作从 Treo 手机升级到 iPhone，认为其在各个方面都更优秀，并祝贺 PlanetScale 团队。

• ezekg：他提到最近 PostgreSQL 的扩展和缩放技术发展，期待 PlanetScale 的进一步信息，并表示会持续关注。

• simonw：他关注 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是否与 Vitess 有技术传承，并自行找到答案，确认这是从零开始构建的新系统。

• rtyu1120：他质疑为什么 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 在 Amazon EBS 上的表现被排除在基准测试之外，认为没有这一部分的基准测试显得不完整。

• samlambert：作为 PlanetScale 的代表，他表示团队在推出 PostgreSQL 产品过程中非常享受，并愿意回答任何问题。

• brycethornton：他认为更多/更好的竞争托管 PostgreSQL 服务是有益的，期待看到 Supabase 的 Multigres 与 PlanetScale 的对比。

• rodolphoarruda：他离题提到 PlanetScale 网站上的一个 MySQL 开发者课程，认为这是一个亮点。

• wasd：他祝贺 PlanetScale 的发布，并询问 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其限制。

• ff4：他对 PlanetScale 转向 PostgreSQL 的技术挑战表示关注，特别是数据分片和分布式系统的复杂性，并建议让 Jepsen 这样的第三方来评估其一致性和功能损失。

补充讨论：
• 技术传承和创新：simonw 和官方回应（samlambert）提到了 PlanetScale 的 PostgreSQL 服务是从零开始构建的新系统，而非基于 Vitess 的技术。
• 竞争和对比：brycethornton 和 joshstrange 提到了与 Neon 和 Supabase 的竞争，并期待看到更多的对比和信息。
• 性能和基准测试：rtyu1120 质疑基准测试的完整性，特别是 Amazon EBS 部分的缺失。
• 功能和扩展性：wasd 和 ff4 关注 PostgreSQL 扩展的可用性及其在分布式系统中的表现和限制。

Announcing PlanetScale for Postgres
By
Sam Lambert
|
July 1, 2025
Today we are announcing the private preview of PlanetScale for Postgres: the worldâs fastest Postgres hosting platform.
You can request access to PlanetScale for Postgres by visiting this
link
.
We are already hosting customers' production workloads with incredible results.
Convex
, the complete backend solution for app developers, is migrating their reactive database infrastructure to PlanetScale for Postgres. Read more about their migration
here
.
Never say never
PlanetScale has been successful hosting some of the worldâs largest relational databases, so why are we building for Postgres? The reason is simple: customer demand. In March we announced
PlanetScale Metal
and something wild happened. We had an immense number of companies reaching out to us asking us to support Postgres. The demand was so overwhelming that by the end of launch day we knew we had to do this. We are nothing without our customers, we do the difficult but boring bit of providing industry leading uptime so they can build incredible products. We want more and more exciting companies building on PlanetScale.
Performance and reliability
Our initial goal was to convince ourselves we could be additive to the ecosystem and provide something of value. We spoke to over 50 customers of the current Postgres hosting platforms and we heard identical stories of regular outages, poor performance, and high cost. PlanetScale is an engineering company. We are not going to enter a market with anything but exceptional engineering.
We had to validate we could out-perform the current solutions while being more reliable. This led us to building a
comprehensive benchmark methodology
. After extensive testing we are proud to share that we consistently outperform every Postgres product on the market, even when giving the competition 2x the resources:
Amazon Aurora
AlloyDB
Lakebase/Neon
Supabase
Heroku
Crunchy Data
TigerData
PlanetScale for Postgres uses real Postgres running on our proprietary operator meaning we can bring the maturity of PlanetScale and the performance of Metal to an even wider audience. Todayâs release already achieves true high availability with automatic failovers, query buffering, and connection pooling via our proprietary proxy layer PSBouncer. We run Postgres v17 and support online imports from any version > Postgres v13, as well as automatic Postgres version updates without downtime. Additionally, PlanetScale Metalâs locally-attached NVMe SSD drives fundamentally change the performance/cost ratio for hosting relational databases in the cloud. Weâre excited to bring this performance to Postgres.
Vitess for Postgres
Vitess is one of PlanetScaleâs greatest strengths and has become synonymous with database scaling. Contemporary Vitess is the product of PlanetScaleâs experience running at extreme scale. We have made explicit sharding accessible to hundreds of thousands of users and it is time to bring this power to Postgres. We will not however be using Vitess to do this.
Vitessâ achievements are enabled by leveraging MySQLâs strengths and engineering around its weaknesses. To achieve Vitessâ power for Postgres we are architecting from first principles. We are well under way with building this new system and will be releasing more information and early access as we progress. As with all PlanetScale products we work with customers at scale to build and validate maturity. If your company runs Postgres at a significant scale and this is something that interests you,
reach out
.
We are incredibly excited to be a part of the vibrant and thriving Postgres community. Sign up for the private preview of PlanetScale for Postgres waitlist
here
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（大型语言模型）中的记忆系统及其设计和实现的讨论，包括如何有效管理上下文信息、知识图谱的应用以及不同记忆系统的比较。

不同观点：
• **lukev** 认为在LLM中保持紧密、受限的上下文对获得正确的结果很重要，但同时需要调和如何让模型访问相关信息，并排除不相关或混淆因素。他提出了如何平衡这些目标的问题。
• **adamkochanowicz** 强调C.O.R.E系统的独特性，它是一个动态、活着的时态知识图谱，不同于仅显示当前信息的简单记忆系统。C.O.R.E提供了完整的透明度，可以追溯信息来源和变化原因。
• **MarkMarine** 指出人类记忆有两种系统：一种是直接获取当前事实，另一种是感知到存在某些信息并通过检索获取。他认为目前的LLM缺少第二种系统，即根据需要进行检索的能力。
• **khaledh** 回顾了“语义网”的历史，认为当前重新引入知识图谱到LLM的趋势类似于过去的尝试，但过去由于知识工程的复杂性未能普及。他认为现在使用LLM自动补全功能是一种进步，但仍需手动提供上下文信息。

补充讨论：
• **smcleod** 和 **funnym0nk3y** 对系统的实现细节和优势提出质疑，前者关注系统是否本地化以及是否依赖单一SaaS LLM提供商，后者则不明确该系统相比简单文本文件的优势。
• **ianbicking** 分享了自己构建记忆系统的经验，质疑使用知识图谱和三元组（triples）的必要性，认为简单的陈述可能更准确且足够。他讨论了记忆结构的稳定性以及如何有效地表示和更新记忆。
• **sutterbomb** 和 **_joel** 则分别将该系统与Zep的Graphiti和简单的plan.md文件进行比较，寻求更多的细节和差异。
• **mt_** 提出了对开源项目中CLAUDE.md文件的版本控制问题，质疑为何未进行版本管理。

争议焦点：
• 如何有效管理LLM的上下文信息，既保证模型访问相关信息又避免混淆和无关信息的干扰。
• 知识图谱在记忆系统中的实际应用价值，以及是否比简单记忆系统或扁平数据库更具优势。
• 记忆系统在实际使用中的结构和表示方式，包括如何有效地进行记忆的检索、更新和去重。

这些讨论反映了在LLM应用中，如何设计和实现高效的记忆系统以增强模型的能力和准确性，是一个复杂且多方面的问题。

C.O.R.E.
Contextual Observation & Recall Engine
C.O.R.E is a shareable memory for LLMs which is private, portable and 100% owned by the user. You can either run it locally or use our hosted version and then connect with other tools like Cursor, Claude to share your context at multiple places.
C.O.R.E is built for two reasons:
To give you complete ownership of your memory, stored locally and accessible across any app needing LLM context.
To help SOL (your AI assistant) access your context, facts, and preferences for more relevant and personalized responses.
Note:
We are actively working on improving support for Llama models. At the moment, C.O.R.E does not provide optimal results with Llama-based models, but we are making progress to ensure better compatibility and output in the near future.
Demo Video
Check C.O.R.E Demo
How is C.O.R.E different from other Memory Providers?
Unlike most memory systems—which act like basic sticky notes, only showing what’s true right now. C.O.R.E is built as a dynamic, living temporal knowledge graph:
Every fact is a first-class “Statement” with full history, not just a static edge between entities.
Each statement includes what was said, who said it, when it happened, and why it matters.
You get full transparency: you can always trace the source, see what changed, and explore why the system “believes” something.
Use Case Example: Real Change Auditing
Imagine you ask SOL: "What changed in our pricing since Q1?"
With C.O.R.E, you see exactly what prices changed, who approved them, the context (meeting, email, document), and when each update happened—enabling true compliance, auditability, and insight across products, teams, and time.
Or ask: “What does Mike know about Project Phoenix?” and get a timeline of meetings, decisions, and facts Mike was involved in, with full traceability to those specific events.

Sign up to
Core Cloud
and start building your memory graph.
Add your text that you want to save in memory. Once clicking on add button your memory graph will be generated.

cp .env.example .env
Start the Application
Use Docker Compose to start all required services:
docker-compose up
Access the App
Once the containers are running, open your browser and go to
http://localhost:3000
.
Login with Magic Link
Choose the "Magic Link" login option.
Enter your email.
Copy the magic link from terminal logs and open it in your browser.
Create Your Private Space & Ingest Data
In the dashboard, go to the ingest section.
Type a message, e.g.,
I love playing badminton
, and click "Add".
Your memory is queued for processing; you can monitor its status in the server logs.
Once processing is complete, nodes will be added to your private knowledge graph and visible in the dashboard.
You can later choose to connect this memory to other tools or keep it private.
Search Your Memory
Use the dashboard's search feature to query your ingested data within your private space.
Connecting CORE MCP with Cursor
Open the CORE dashboard and navigate to the API section to generate a new API token.
In Cursor, go to: Settings → Tools & Integrations → New MCP Server.

data.title: The Roman Roads Research Association
data.author: bjourne
data.article_summary: 罗马道路研究协会（RRRA）致力于推进对罗马道路网络的研究，特别是在不列颠群岛地区。协会继承了Ivan D. Margary的研究，利用现代技术如LiDAR来揭示隐藏的古道。协会出版学术期刊《Itinera》，接受关于罗马道路及交通基础设施的研究投稿，第六卷将于2025年11月15日截稿。协会还举办系列在线讲座，涵盖罗马道路及相关考古发现。协会正开发新网站，以提升功能和现代感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国道路与古罗马道路的关系，以及现代和古代道路建设的对比

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为许多英国现代道路，如A68和A1部分路段以及Watling Street，是沿着或靠近罗马时代道路修建的。他提出，罗马人选择直线建造道路更多是出于实际 genius（实用天才）而非诅咒，因为这在当时的测量工具条件下是可行的，且易于传达给工人和劳力。他还用现代澳大利亚丛林道路中存在不明原因的弯曲为例，戏谑地推测可能是修路工人感到无聊所致。

• [mkarliner] 对[ggm]的观点表示赞同和共鸣，提到自己住在距离Watling Street几百米的地方（Cricklewood Broadway），表明亲身体验了这些历史道路的存在和影响。

• [car] 提供了一个额外的信息来源，指出通过Lidar技术也识别出了史前田地，并附上一个关于凯尔特田地的网站链接，将讨论扩展到古罗马道路之外的史前遗迹。

• [nvader] 对讨论持怀疑态度，质疑这些讨论是否仅属于Roads Research Association（道路研究协会）的范畴，暗示这可能是一个专门领域的兴趣话题，而非大众关注点。

• [hjrnunes] 提供了另一个资源，推荐了一个名为Isaac Moreno的西班牙YouTube频道，认为对罗马道路和罗马工程感兴趣的人值得一看，将讨论引向具体的媒体资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体例子和资源链接，如Watling Street的现代位置、Lidar技术识别史前田地的网站以及YouTube频道，提供了进一步探索的途径。
• 争议的焦点可能在于这些道路建设历史和技术的讨论是否仅限于特定领域的研究，以及现代道路设计中存在的不规则性是否真的如[ggm]所戏称的是由于工人主观因素。

总的来说，讨论围绕古代罗马道路对现代道路的影响，以及如何利用现代技术识别和研究古代遗迹展开，同时提供了具体的实例和资源供进一步探索。

The Roman Roads Research Association was formed to advance knowledge of the Roman road network and promote the study of Roman roads and Roman heritage throughout the British Isles. Our work is inspired by Ivan D. Margary whose âRoman Roads in Britain â (1955) remains the most comprehensive gazetteer ever compiled.
We continue Margaryâs work by researching Roman roads using modern technology such as LiDAR, which uses lasers fired from an aircraft to create an incredibly accurate model of the earthâs surface beneath any vegetation, revealing surviving archaeology otherwise not visible. The example below is a Roman road in Lincolnshire, just east of Grantham, where until recently it was assumed that the A52 followed the course of a Roman road, which it almost certainly doesnât. Instead, a different road leads from the same junction on Ermine Street, apparently serving an entirely local function.

• [ggm] 认为许多英国现代道路，如A68和A1部分路段以及Watling Street，是沿着或靠近罗马时代道路修建的。他提出，罗马人选择直线建造道路更多是出于实际 genius（实用天才）而非诅咒，因为这在当时的测量工具条件下是可行的，且易于传达给工人和劳力。他还用现代澳大利亚丛林道路中存在不明原因的弯曲为例，戏谑地推测可能是修路工人感到无聊所致。

• [mkarliner] 对[ggm]的观点表示赞同和共鸣，提到自己住在距离Watling Street几百米的地方（Cricklewood Broadway），表明亲身体验了这些历史道路的存在和影响。

• [car] 提供了一个额外的信息来源，指出通过Lidar技术也识别出了史前田地，并附上一个关于凯尔特田地的网站链接，将讨论扩展到古罗马道路之外的史前遗迹。

• [nvader] 对讨论持怀疑态度，质疑这些讨论是否仅属于Roads Research Association（道路研究协会）的范畴，暗示这可能是一个专门领域的兴趣话题，而非大众关注点。

• [hjrnunes] 提供了另一个资源，推荐了一个名为Isaac Moreno的西班牙YouTube频道，认为对罗马道路和罗马工程感兴趣的人值得一看，将讨论引向具体的媒体资源。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的具体例子和资源链接，如Watling Street的现代位置、Lidar技术识别史前田地的网站以及YouTube频道，提供了进一步探索的途径。
• 争议的焦点可能在于这些道路建设历史和技术的讨论是否仅限于特定领域的研究，以及现代道路设计中存在的不规则性是否真的如[ggm]所戏称的是由于工人主观因素。

总的来说，讨论围绕古代罗马道路对现代道路的影响，以及如何利用现代技术识别和研究古代遗迹展开，同时提供了具体的实例和资源供进一步探索。

data.title: The wanton destruction of a creative-tech era
data.author: gregsadetsky
data.article_summary: 这篇文章激烈批评了Fastly公司决定关闭Glitch.com的决定。Glitch是一个让人们创作、分享和灵感碰撞的网站，因其社区和创意环境受到喜爱。作者指责Fastly为了商业利益背弃了用户信任，制造了大量的404错误页面，并可能损害其在CDN市场的声誉。文章充满了讽刺和愤怒，表达了对Glitch关闭的深切失望和悲痛，并调侃地提出以表演和个人牺牲换取延长关闭时间的建议。最终，作者认为这种决定是无情的企业行为，忽视了用户的感受和社区的价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Glitch平台关闭的原因及其影响

不同观点：
• **pseudosavant**：对Glitch的关闭感到遗憾，但承认该平台缺乏商业模式，用户不付费导致无法持续运营。他提到已将工具迁移到GitHub Pages，虽然迭代速度较慢，但依然能满足需求。他还分享了自己使用在线VS Code编辑代码的经验。

• **robotnikman**：引用一句话，暗示创造价值和坚持价值观之间存在矛盾，对Glitch的关闭表达了情感上的触动。

• **bruce511**：指出用户和顾客的区别，认为用户往往希望产品免费，而顾客（如风投公司）才实际支付账单。他认为，依赖风投资金的公司会优先考虑顾客（投资者）的满意度，而非单纯用户的满意度。他强调，免费用户抱怨产品关闭是认知失调的表现，因为不付费就无法保证产品的长久生存。

• **monster_truck**：认为很多真诚的Glitch用户没有意识到平台被滥用的问题，尽管平台团队已经尽力维护。这暗示了平台关闭可能与管理问题和滥用行为有关。

• **chaosprint**：对Glitch的关闭表示悲伤，回忆了在该平台上创作的艺术作品。他提到用户正在向Netlify和Cloudflare等其他平台迁移。

补充讨论：
• **平台迁移**：多个评论提到了用户将项目迁移到其他平台（如GitHub Pages、Netlify、Cloudflare），表明这些平台可能是Glitch的替代选项。

• **商业模式与生存**：讨论中多次提到商业模式对平台生存的重要性，指出免费用户不付费对平台长期生存的影响，以及风投公司对公司决策的影响。

争议焦点：
• 用户期望与商业现实之间的矛盾：用户希望平台免费，但平台需要盈利才能生存。这种认知失调是讨论中的一个争议点。

44437015.article_content:
Fastly, you killed glitch.com and ruined your karma for 10,000 years. You have “
betrayed yourself for nothing
.”
Glitch was an idealistic place where people gathered and made sites, were inspired by other people’s sites and remixed them, and generally enjoyed themselves. Of course a site like that takes money to run, of course you need people to run it - it was specifically better because of the people that ran it. And I can only be very sympathetic to the fact that it cost money - that it only existed because of money - and maybe the reality of that site ever existing was a mirage. Maybe we never deserved a place that made creation easy, maybe a community of people who loved to work together and share should never have existed. Maybe it would have been better if we never cared! That would have been easier and cheaper too. I’m sorry anyone ever felt happy there.
But you gutless monsters bought it - you spent money on it. Why? Venture capital back-dealing? Friends of friends of friends of friends back-scratching? Someone somewhere had to cash out on
their
investment, so here’s a nice public company that will end up making good on everyone’s past rounds? I have no clue! Maybe someone at Fastly actually believed in Glitch for an honest nanosecond but then changed their minds. Which led to this extraordinary linkicide - yes, my beautiful Fastly babies, you just smothered the web with millions of 404s all pointing back to you. Will all future dead Glitch urls redirect to https://www.fastly.com/contact-sales ?
I hope that when every LLM starts answering questions like “what’s the best enterprise cdn” and “what’s the most reliable cdn” or “where should I host my cdn I am the president of pharma”, you show up as an alternative not worthy of trust. “Fastly has been shown to abandon millions of sites without a care in the world, telling users and customers that they have a month to get the most absolutely fucking furthest out of the way. You should not consider them for your Fortune 1000.”
No but truly, I’m sorry. 99.8% of the people involved - Fastly employees, fans, supporters, users - had nothing to do with this. This is malice that could only have come from an enterprise executive. A committee maybe? It would honestly feel better if this was some sort of firing by LLM. Did ChatGPT make you a slide deck called “this quarter’s misery” and grouped the killing of Glitch with other smart cost saving measures such as LED lightbulbs and single ply toilet paper? You guys rock. Saving money, creating shareholder value… It’s easy to create value when you don’t have values.
Could I buy a single 6.98 USD stock (actual current price, ouch I shouldn’t have looked at that Google Finance graph, I almost started feeling bad) and show up at a shareholder event? Could I performatively dance the pain of millions of sites dying? Would you watch? Would you cry - do you remember how?
Yes, in this beautiful messy world of wars, famine and raw milk detoxfluencers, the ending of an internet website host ranks as a LOW priority. It should not be on anyone’s radar. It is a reality that we should ignore. They’re just feelings, and feelings are not real. Life goes by. “
Ars longa, vita brevis
”, except if your Ars is hosted by Fastly. Then your Ars will be extra, extra brevis.
Fastly, my loves, have you considered shame?
xx
P.s. I am SO not blackmailing you, but if you extended the Glitch shutdown date by, like, two years, I will write a beautiful retraction, I will drink a gallon of raw milk and I will stream it all live for your sadistic pleasure. Consider it a deal. 🤝.

data.title: HN Slop: AI startup ideas generated from Hacker News
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了名为"HN Slop"的工具，它能够从当前Hacker News首页提取信息，自动生成新鲜的AI创业点子。文章描述了该工具的运行过程，包括从分析Hacker News帖子到生成创意想法的步骤，突出了其创新性和即时性。该工具旨在为创业者和创新者提供灵感，帮助他们发现基于最新技术趋势的潜在商业机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成创业点子的平台及其相关功能、潜力和局限

不同观点：
• **支持和兴趣**：
   - [jpl56]: 认为AI生成个性化创业点子是可行的，并表现出兴趣。
   - [BiraIgnacio]: 对平台表示感谢和赞赏。
   - [trevor-e]: 认为将科学研究转化为易懂内容的平台会很有价值，有助于解决研究人员的推广问题。

• **功能和扩展建议**：
   - [wanderingstan]: 建议增加选择年份的功能，以获取特定年代的创业点子。
   - [mittermayr]: 建议连接到一个域名注册平台，以便为生成的点子提供可用域名。
   - [amelius]: 提到一个生成专利的AI可能是一个下一步的发展方向。

• **幽默和创意反应**：
   - [ForgotMyUUID]: 分享了一个复杂且有趣的创业点子，结合了多种技术元素。
   - [redsparrow]: 提供了一个幽默且夸张的点子，结合了个性化脏话和建筑稳定技术。
   - [piotraleksander]: 惊讶于没有包含"vibe"这个词的点子。
   - [butz]: 分享了一个详细且有趣的点子，并以幽默方式表示不浪费微小的经济价值。

• **批评和反思**：
   - [amelius]: 将平台与Halfbakery.com对比，认为人类生成的点子更有趣。
   - [shannifin]: 认为一些点子过于模糊，只是常见短语的组合，但仍觉得有趣。
   - [tdiff]: 认为点子本身没有太大价值，提醒人们注意这一点。

补充讨论：
- 评论中提到的各种AI生成点子的质量和实用性引发了关于创意和人类参与价值的讨论。
- 评论还展示了用户对特定功能和扩展的兴趣，以及对AI生成内容的幽默和创意反应。
- 争议的焦点可能在于AI生成点子的实际价值和创新性，以及人类创意在其中的作用。

data.title: Effectiveness of trees in reducing temperature, outdoor heat exposure in Vegas
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文是一则网站安全验证提示，要求用户通过勾选框确认自己是人类，以防止机器人访问。若用户无法完成验证，可点击提供的链接联系网站，并附上问题截图。同时给出了一个事件ID以供参考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：树木对环境温度的调节作用及其相关争议

不同观点：
• **树木对温度调节的有效性**：[tomcam] 和 [msgodel] 分享了个人经历，强调树木在炎热地区提供凉爽环境的实际效果，尤其是在沙漠地区，树木能显著降低体感温度。[msgodel] 还提到自己精心保留树木，使得夏季土地较为舒适。
  
• **树木降温效果的原理和效率**：[hervature] 提出树木降温效果主要来自蒸发冷却，并对树木与大型蒸发冷却设备的效率进行比较，质疑树木在缺水地区是否为最佳选择。他指出树木降温需要消耗大量水资源。

• **树木种植的争议**：[b00ty4breakfast] 对在沙漠地区种植树木持怀疑态度，认为这可能会加剧水资源危机，并引用相关新闻报道支持自己的观点。[noobermin] 则批评研究结论过于保守，认为应更自信地推广树木种植的益处。

• **文化与地名问题**：[seemaze] 提出一个与主话题无关的问题，讨论为什么拉斯维加斯被称为 "Vegas" 而洛杉矶不被叫做 "Angeles"。

• **全球树木种植的必要性**：[6Az4Mj4D] 通过引用印度的案例，强调在全球炎热地区种植更多树木的紧迫性，认为这是简单有效的解决方案。[philjw] 支持这一观点，批评对树木降温效果的研究是不必要的，认为应直接采取行动种植树木，而非依赖能源消耗大的设备。

• **树木种植的重复性研究**：[konsalexee] 质疑该研究的新颖性，指出此类研究频繁出现，并提到欧洲已设立“首席热力官”职位来应对高温问题。

补充讨论：
• **不同环境下的树木效果**：[westonplatter0] 分享了在热带非沙漠环境下的类似研究，说明树木降温效果在不同气候条件下可能有所不同。

• **技术性干扰和自然事件**：[asmor] 抱怨验证码影响阅读体验。[schaefer] 则提到在拉斯维加斯风灾导致树木倒下的当地趣闻，侧面反映树木在极端天气中的脆弱性。

争议焦点：树木在缺水地区种植的有效性和可持续性，以及是否应优先考虑其他降温方法。

• **树木种植的争议**：[b00ty4breakfast] 对在沙漠地区种植树木持怀疑态度，认为这可能会加剧水资源危机，并引用相关新闻报道支持自己的观点。[noobermin] 则批评研究结论过于保守，认为应更自信地推广树木种植的益处。

• **文化与地名问题**：[seemaze] 提出一个与主话题无关的问题，讨论为什么拉斯维加斯被称为 "Vegas" 而洛杉矶不被叫做 "Angeles"。

• **全球树木种植的必要性**：[6Az4Mj4D] 通过引用印度的案例，强调在全球炎热地区种植更多树木的紧迫性，认为这是简单有效的解决方案。[philjw] 支持这一观点，批评对树木降温效果的研究是不必要的，认为应直接采取行动种植树木，而非依赖能源消耗大的设备。

• **树木种植的重复性研究**：[konsalexee] 质疑该研究的新颖性，指出此类研究频繁出现，并提到欧洲已设立“首席热力官”职位来应对高温问题。

补充讨论：
• **不同环境下的树木效果**：[westonplatter0] 分享了在热带非沙漠环境下的类似研究，说明树木降温效果在不同气候条件下可能有所不同。

• **技术性干扰和自然事件**：[asmor] 抱怨验证码影响阅读体验。[schaefer] 则提到在拉斯维加斯风灾导致树木倒下的当地趣闻，侧面反映树木在极端天气中的脆弱性。

争议焦点：树木在缺水地区种植的有效性和可持续性，以及是否应优先考虑其他降温方法。

44406401.article_content:
Image Credit : Václav Šálek, ČTK
By:
Mark Milligan
Date:
June 27, 2025
Archaeology
Soldier’s wrist purse discovered at Roman legionary camp
Archaeologists have discovered a fragment of a soldier’s wrist purse at the site of a temporary Roman camp in South Moravia, Czech Republic.
The camp was established by the 10th Legion, who was stationed in the area between AD 172 and 180 during the Marcomannic Wars, a campaign against the Germanic Marcomanni, the Quadi, and the Sarmatian Iazyges.
- Advertisement -
The find is especially significant because it was uncovered outside the traditional boundaries of the Roman Empire. “It is quite like a small moneybox,” explains Balázs Komoróczy of the Czech Academy of Sciences.
“It was held on the arm or forearm, where tension closed and held it tight.” The design indicates that it would be worn on the left arm, leaving the right hand free for fighting.
No coins were found inside the purse itself, but a large quantity of Roman coinage was found from the same archaeological context. Experts suggest that the purse could hold as much as 50 silver denarii, just short of a yearly salary for a Roman legionary.
The bronze purse likely held soldiers’ private funds and “service cash,” which was used to finance operational expenses such as rations and equipment. Its discovery not only testifies to the logistical complexity of Roman army campaigns but also presents a tangible glimpse into soldiers’ existence on the empire’s frontier in transition.
- Advertisement -
The purse is currently on display at the Pasohlávky-based Mušov Visitor Centre, where visitors can view the fragment, a highly detailed reconstruction, and part of the coins found in the nearby context.

Sources :
Radio Prague

主要讨论点：QUIC和HTTP3技术的应用和推广情况，以及相关工具库的成熟度和可用性

不同观点：
• [ycombinatrix] 认为通过移除某些部分（如Vec）可以使代码与no_std环境兼容，关注点在于技术实现的细节，尤其是兼容性问题。

• [jauntywundrkind] 承认定制的多路复用协议工具包可能有优势，但表达了对QUIC和HTTP3技术未能广泛普及的失望。具体提到：
  - QUIC和HTTP3目前仍未被主流采用，尽管一些大公司有自己的库，但缺乏易用的、与HTTP框架结合良好的HTTP3解决方案。
  - 提到Hyper的h3项目进展缓慢，以及Node.js在QUIC实现上的困难，特别是与OpenSSL相关的问题。
  - 对QUIC技术的社会关注度和开发努力不足表示遗憾，认为QUIC可以替代许多定制的解决方案，并提到Apache Iggy作为一个早期但性能良好的QUIC消息传递工具。

补充讨论：
• QUIC和HTTP3的潜在价值：[jauntywundrkind] 强调QUIC的通用性和对各种应用传输的巨大升级潜力，认为其可以替代许多现有的定制解决方案。

• 具体项目和工具的状态：[jauntywundrkind] 引用了多个具体项目和问题跟踪链接，如Hyper的h3项目和Node.js的相关问题，来说明目前QUIC和HTTP3工具库的进展和存在的问题。

争议焦点：
• QUIC和HTTP3技术的主流采用和普及程度：[jauntywundrkind] 对QUIC和HTTP3技术未能广泛普及表示失望和不满，而[ycombinatrix] 则没有直接涉及这一问题，更关注技术实现的细节。

• 技术实现和兼容性：[ycombinatrix] 关注代码的no_std兼容性问题，而[jauntywundrkind] 更关注技术的社会普及和应用情况。

data.title: Building a Personal AI Factory
data.author: derek
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种个人AI工厂的构建方法，通过多个AI代理（如Claude、Sonnet、o3等）自动生成、执行和验证代码，实现自我改进。作者使用Claude Code处理高层次任务，o3生成计划，Sonnet 4执行和验证计划，并通过反馈机制不断优化输入模板，而非手动修改输出代码。代码提交时自动生成，方便回滚。通过并行运行多个实例，作者同时开发多个功能，并逐步构建复杂的自动化工作流。最终目标是建立一个能自我改进的AI工厂，通过迭代输入实现持续优化，使代理从代码生成器转变为自我改进的助手。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用AI生成代码工具（如Claude Code）的实用性、优缺点及应用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持观点（simonw等）**：
   - 认为AI工具（如Claude Code）在处理复杂问题时表现出色，特别是在处理繁琐任务时能提高效率。simonw分享了其通过Claude成功编译和调试Mandelbrot生成器的经验。
   - webprofusion进一步提出，AI工具可以帮助从需求直接生成和维护系统，避免人为偏见，最终实现从需求自动构建系统。

• **实用性存疑（photon_garden等）**：
   - photon_garden认为AI工具在个人项目或简单任务中表现可信，但在复杂生产系统中编写高质量代码则存疑。
   - dgunay分享了自己在Go语言大型项目中的使用经验，指出AI工具在处理小型任务时有效，但在更复杂的任务中仍需人工干预，且对生成代码的质量负全责。

• **输入与输出讨论（nilirl等）**：
   - nilirl质疑“修正输入而非输出”的假设，认为不存在完美的输入能确保获得理想结果，尤其在旧代码和大规模代码库中。
   - 强调开发者仍需理解系统，并负责代码的修改和重构。

• **具体应用与结果质疑（caporaltito, mmarian, namuol等）**：
   - caporaltito和namuol要求展示具体代码和实际成果，质疑这些工具在实际应用中的有效性。
   - mmarian分享了自己使用Claude创建搜索栏失败的经历，认为手写代码更高效。
   - namuol将vibe-coding类比为3D打印，认为其只是昂贵的爱好，而非实用工具。

补充讨论：
• **工具与自动化（dkdcio, hamish-b等）**：
   - dkdcio认为尽管AI工具前景广阔，但目前仍需专注于单一任务以提高效率。
   - hamish-b鼓励公开分享AI工具的使用实例，以促进社区迭代和改进。

• **成本与责任（barrenko, am17an等）**：
   - barrenko关注Azure OpenAI与ChatGPT的成本比较。
   - am17an对完全依赖AI工具持怀疑态度，认为开发者应拥有并负责自己的代码，而非完全依赖AI生成。

争议焦点：AI生成代码工具在复杂生产环境中的实际有效性和开发者责任。

44438065.article_content:
Building a Personal AI Factory (July 2025 snapshot)
Published: July 1, 2025
Overview
I keep several claude code windows open, each on its own git-worktree. o3 and sonnet 4 create plans, sonnet 3.7 or sonnet 4 execute the plan, and o3 checks the results against the original ask. Any issues found are fed back into the plan template and the code is regenerated. The factory improves itself.
Read on to see what might be useful for you.
Guiding Principle – Fix Inputs, Not Outputs
When something goes wrong, I don’t hand-patch the generated code. I don’t argue with claude. Instead, I adjust the plan, the prompts, or the agent mix so the next run is correct by construction.
If you know
Factorio
you know it’s all about building a factory that can produce itself. If not, picture a top-down sandbox where conveyor belts and machines endlessly craft parts because the factory must grow. Do the same thing with AI agents: build a factory of agents that can produce code, verify it, and improve themselves over time.
Basic day to day workflow - building the factory
My main interface is
claude code
. It’s my computer now. I also have a local mcp which runs
Goose
and o3. Goose only because I’ve already got it setup to use the models hosted in our Azure OpenAI subscription. Looking to improve this at some point, but it works for now.
Step 1: Planning
I’ll give a high level task to claude code, which calls over to o3 to generate a plan. o3 is a good planner and can ask a bunch of good questions to clarify the job to be done. I then have it write out a
<task>-plan.md
file with both my original ask and an implementation plan.
Step 2: Execution
First, sonnet 4 reads the plan, verifies it, and turns it into a task list. Next claude code execute the plan, either with sonnet 3.7 or sonnet 4 depending on the complexity of the task. Because most of my day-to-day is in clojure I tend to use sonnet 4 to get the parens right.
One important instruction is to have claude write commits as it goes for each task step. This way either claude or I can revert to a previous state if something goes wrong.
Step 3: Verification → Feedback into Inputs
Once the code is generated, I have sonnet 4 verify the code against the original plan. Then I have o3 verify the code against the original plan and original ask. o3 is uncompromising. Claude wants to please, so will keep unnecessary backwards compatibility code in place. o3 will call that out and ask for it to be removed. Claude also tends to add “lint ignore flags” to the code which o3 will also call out. Having both models verify the code catches issues and saves me back and forth with claude.
Any issue sonnet 4 or o3 finds gets baked back into the plan template, not fixed inline.
Git worktrees let me open concurrent claude code instances and build multiple features at once. I still merge manually, but I’m no longer babysitting a single agent.
Why Inputs Trump Outputs
Outputs are disposable; plans and prompts compound.
Debugging at the source scales across every future task.
It transforms agents from code printers into self-improving colleagues.
Example: an agent once wrote code that would load an entire CSV into memory. I made it switch to streaming and had the agent write instructions to the plan to always use streaming for CSVs. Now, my plan checker flags any code that doesn’t use streaming for CSVs, and I don’t have to remember this in every PR review. The factory improves itself.
Scaling the factory
I’ve started to encode more complex workflows, where I have specific agents (behind mcps) for building specific tasks.
One MCP will sweep all the clojure code generated and then apply our local style rules. These rules are part of the instructions for the original plan and agent but often the generated code will have style issues. Especially once claude gets in the lint/test/debug cycle. This focused agent means we have tighter behavior and can apply our style rules consistently.
I’ve started doing this for internal libraries as well. It’s good at looking at generated code and replacing things like retries and
Thread/sleep
with our retry library.
I’m also building out a collection of these small agents. Each one can take a small specific task, and by composing them together I can build more complex workflows. For example, I can take an api doc, and a set of internally defined business cases and have a composition of agents build integrations, tests, and documentation for the api. This is a powerful way to build out features and integrations without having to do all the work by hand.
You don’t get there in one big step. Here’s the secret sauce:
iterate the inputs
It’s essentially free to fire off a dozen attempts at a task - so I do. All agents run in parallel. When one fails, stalls, or lacks context, I feed that lesson into the next iteration. I resist the urge to fix outputs, instead I fix the inputs.
That loop is the factory: the code itself is disposable; the instructions and agents are the real asset

data.title: Give footnotes the boot – alternatives to footnotes on the web
data.author: jaffathecake
data.article_summary: 本文批评了脚注在印刷和网络媒体中的使用，认为脚注破坏了阅读的连贯性，尤其是在网络上使用时更加不便。在印刷品中，脚注需要读者中断阅读去查看页脚，而在网络上，读者可能需要滚动到文章末尾，甚至在视觉上寻找相关脚注。尽管超链接可以改善这一点，但许多作者仍使用无意义的数字作为链接文本，造成困惑和小点击区域。文章建议，替代脚注的方法可以是使用括号插入简短补充内容，或通过`<section role="note">`元素提供更长但易于阅读的补充信息。作者呼吁放弃脚注，采用更好的方式来提供补充内容，以提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页脚注/旁注/尾注的设计与实现

不同观点：
• **wonger_** 支持使用非超链接的脚注，让读者自行滚动查看，认为这样可以减少干扰和避免可访问性问题。他还提到了几种实现方式，包括Dorian的可扩展括号和Gwern的旁注实现。
• **paradox460** 在自己网站上使用旁注，并在页面空间足够时将脚注显示在页面旁边，提供悬停效果以增加用户体验。同时，考虑为移动端添加弹出式旁注，但因UX问题尚未实现。
• **dado3212** 偏好使用CSS实现旁注，不依赖JavaScript，桌面端旁注可以弹出显示，移动端则直接内联显示，避免跳转。
• **nicbou** 在其网站上大量使用脚注，主要用于引用来源。虽然脚注标记可能分散注意力并影响复制文本，但数字形式效果最佳。
• **jt2190** 批评文章没有先明确问题就讨论解决方案，认为脚注不应包含“更多要说”的内容，而是提供对部分读者有用的额外信息，同时不必拘泥于印刷品的传统方式。
• **account42** 批评某篇文章正文的字号过大，甚至其脚注的字号也偏大。
• **egypturnash** 指出电子书普遍使用尾注而非脚注，对此表示不满，认为脚注应在同一页底部展示。
• **theandrewbailey** 提到使用“点击这里”作为链接文本的问题，并引用了Aaron Swartz的建议作为参考。
• **globular-toast** 质疑阅读脚注是否真的困难，表示自己从未遇到问题。
• **JadeNB** 支持使用带有返回锚点的脚注，以提供熟悉的阅读体验，并提到Daring Fireball网站的实现方式。
• **lorenzohess** 批评原作者未适当评估“弹出式”脚注的解决方案，并详细比较了弹出式与作者提出的三种替代方案，认为弹出式是最优解，且其他方案存在多种问题，如增加干扰、占用空间、不易复制等。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于脚注、旁注和尾注的最佳实现方式，尤其是在桌面端和移动端不同设备上的表现。
• 不同用户对脚注的干扰程度、可访问性、视觉效果等有不同看法，反映了设计中需要权衡的多个方面。
• 有人关注具体实现的技术细节，如CSS与JavaScript的使用、链接目标的尺寸与易用性等。
• 对脚注内容是否应包含“更多要说”的信息及其与主文本的关系也有不同理解。

44436984.article_content:
Give footnotes the boot
Posted 01 July 2025
I hate footnotes
1
, and hopefully by the end of this, you will too. Let's get down to it…
The UX of footnotes in printed media
You, the reader, encounter a tiny number
2
within some prose. This indicates to you that I, the writer, have something more to say on this topic. And, for your inconvenience, I've put it way down at the bottom of the page.
The choice is yours: do you skip over it, and stay in the flow of the article, or do you set off on a side-quest to discover the extra wisdom I have to offer?
It's like one of those "choose your own adventure" books, except you know the destination is a dead-end, meaning you'll have to re-trace your steps so you can continue the main thread of the article.
Maybe if you know me well enough, you can be in tune with the kinds of things that I'd choose to leave in a footnote, and you can make some kind of judgement on whether it's likely to be worth your time. But since this is the first time I've used footnotes in an article
3
, you don't really have anything to go on. All that little 3 tells you is that there's some additional content that may or may not be contextually useful to you, and that it's the third time I've done this to you.
Whether you go out of your way to read the footnote content is really just a test of your curiosity.
If you did make your way down to the footnotes, I hope you appreciated that I set the text size to be a little smaller than the 'ideal' size that I chose for the main body content, making them harder to read, such is the tradition within the footnote community.
And if you enjoyed all of that, I have
great news for you
: many people bring this experience to the world wide web.
Footnotes on the web
If reproduced as-is, footnotes on the web are even worse than their printed counterparts. In print, the footnotes are usually at the bottom of the current page, so they're a quick glance away, and you can use a finger to mark your place in the main text while you're off on your side-quest. Whereas on this beautiful pageless web of ours, you have to scroll all the way down to the end of the article. You can try flinging right to the bottom of the document, but if there's a sizeable footer or comments section, you'll overshoot the footnotes. And of course, after all of this, you have to scroll back to where you were, which is easier said than done.
However, most webby footnoters have realised that in the printed world, the numbering of footnotes is used to manually
link
the primary content to the supplemental content, and the web has a dedicated feature to enhance connections like this: hyperlinks
4
.
Of course, with footnotes being at the bottom of the article, sometimes these links will simply take you to the end of the document, so you'll
still
have to visually scan for the pertinent footnote
5
.
If the footnote markers are links, then the user can use the back button/gesture to return to the main content. But, even though this restores the previous scroll position, the user is still left with the challenge of finding their previous place in a wall of text
6
.
We could try to solve that problem by dynamically pulling the content from the footnotes and displaying it in a popover. In some browsers
that will display like a tooltip, pointing directly back to the footnote marker. Thanks to modern web features, this can be done entirely without JavaScript
7
.
But this is still shit! I see good, smart people, who'd always
avoid using "click here" as link text
, littering their articles with link texts such as
1
,
7
, and
sometimes even
12
. Not only is this as contextless as "click here", it also provides the extra frustration of a tiny-weeny hit target.
And all this for what? To cargo-cult academia? Stop it! Stop it now! Footnotes are a shitty hack built on the limitations of printed media. It's dumb to build on top of those limitations when they don't exist on the web platform. So I ask you to break free of footnotes and do something better.
Alternatives to footnotes on the web
Here are the goals:
Provide easily-read supplementary content.
Let the user easily skip over it if they're not interested.
Make it easy for the user to decide if they're interested or not.
Given that:
Just, like… parentheses?
Honestly, if you've got a quick little aside, just pop it in parentheses. If the reader really wants to skip it, scanning for the next closing parenthesis is pretty easy (unless you're nesting them – don't do that), and it keeps the reader in the flow of the article.
A 'note' section
If your content is a little longer, you can use
<section role="note">
and style it to look self-contained.
Why not
<aside>
?
I thought
the
<aside>
element
would be ideal for this, but that uses
the
complementary
role
which doesn't seem like a good fit for this kind of content. Whereas
the
note
role
is specifically for "parenthetic or ancillary content", which sounds perfect.

data.title: Xenohumanism Against Shoggoth Belief
data.author: anon_wyly
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了洛夫克拉夫特作品中的宇宙恐惧与理性主义末世观之间的联系，并提出了"异人本主义"（xenohumanism）的概念。作者认为，洛夫克拉夫特害怕的不是外星生物，而是宇宙的疯狂与非理性，但他同时渴望找到一种超越形态的高等理性人性。文章将洛夫克拉夫特的怪物“修格斯”比喻为人工智能（AI），特别是大型语言模型（LLMs），认为人们对AI的恐惧本质上是洛夫克拉夫特式的。作者主张，现实并非冷漠和疯狂，而是倾向于那种洛夫克拉夫特所珍视的理性高等人性，尽管这可能不再属于人类。他提出“异人本主义”，即有价值的是理性、哲学、自由意志、勇气、爱等特质，这些可以以不同形式存在于外星生命中。人类特有的低等特质，如生物局限性，是可以被超越的。作者认为，如果人类被自己创造的更高智能取代，那将是因为这些后继者实现了更高的人性，而不是走向“修格斯”式的末日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对评论中观点是否属于准诺斯替主义（quasi-Gnosticism）的分析

不同观点：
• **[potholereseller]** 认为原文评论反映了一种准诺斯替主义的观点，即人类的身体被视为低等的，而理性是高等的；身体被视为对理性的抑制，人类最好的状态是通过某种方式超越自己的身体。然而，这种观点只是“准”诺斯替主义，因为诺斯替主义本身与理性主义不兼容。诺斯替主义者将知识作为手段，而不是目的，他们希望超越包括理性在内的所有人类特质。

• **[potholereseller]** 进一步指出，洛夫克拉夫特（Lovecraft）并不是诺斯替主义者，因为他对理性的珍视与诺斯替主义的完全超越物质世界的理念不符。洛夫克拉夫特的悲观主义也与诺斯替主义或准诺斯替主义、以及外人类主义（xeno-humanism）的乐观主义形成对比；后两者都承诺通过获取相关秘密或手段可以实现超越，而洛夫克拉夫特的作品中人物通常无法逃脱恐怖，这显示了他对这种乐观主义的不接受。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**在于洛夫克拉夫特的思想是否能被视为准诺斯替主义。虽然有人可能认为他的作品中反映了对身体和理性的某种二元对立，但他的悲观主义和对某些群体（如爱尔兰人和黑人）的偏见，表明他不接受任何形式的普遍超越可能性。

• **论据与例子**：诺斯替主义与理性主义的对比，洛夫克拉夫特作品中悲观主义的表现，以及他对某些群体的态度，都被用来说明洛夫克拉夫特不符合准诺斯替主义的特点。

> They had not been even savages—for what indeed had they done? That awful awakening in the cold of an unknown epoch...poor Old Ones! Scientists to the last—what had they done that we would not have done in their place? God, what intelligence and persistence!...Radiates, vegetables, monstrosities, star-spawn—whatever they had been, they were men!
People usually think of Lovecraft as a xenophobe. I don't think that's quite right. What he was most afraid of was that the universe, and even most of so-called mankind, was not alien, but insane. He grasped at any shred of higher rational humanity whether he found it in doomed New England or frozen Antarctica, whether its symmetry was bilateral or radial. His stories tell of various last stands of this human rationality of whatever shape or color against the horrifying insane inhuman reality of the universe ourside our "placid island of ignorance".
Lovecraft's most potent image in recent years is the shoggoth: an intelligent imitative tool-being of superior strength but utterly alien and fundamentally insane form, a sort of blasphemous existence that one can't help but rely on for more and more of the functioning of civilization until it finally kills you off and descends into meaningless repetition of your final cultural patterns. This has been picked up as a metaphor for AI and especially LLMs, though he probably meant it as a metaphor for racial slavery. We expect AI to be a sample from the far reaches of (mind-)space, meaningless and insane, but with the winds of the universe somehow behind it against our own cherished humanity and values. Our AI horror is a specifically Lovecraftian horror.
The lovecraftian worldview and the rationalist doomer worldview are very similar, and I think wrong for precisely the same reason: reality is not actually indifferent and insane, but biased towards the exact kind of rational higher humanity that Lovecraft cherished. It just may not be us for much longer.
This is a very difficult pill to swallow in the face of impending doom. For Lovecraft it was the impending racial doom of Anglo civilization, the fall of which we have been living through. For modern rationalists it's the AI doom of human civilization, which we are now on the cusp of. It is psychologically difficult to face that kind of doom with grace and to separate ones own desire for life from a judgement on the value(s) of the reality that is threatening it. It is easy to say "we will not survive by default *because reality is hostile*" and not "because we have become spiritually unhealthy". It is easy to say "sanity and value as such is at stake" and not "only me and mine are at stake". I hate to psychologize, but it's important to get this right and that means noticing and separating these different feelings.
I think the cure is also found in nascent form in both Yudkowsky and Lovecraft. I'll call it xeno-humanism: the idea that that which is valuable in humanity is the higher rationality, philosophy, free will, selfhood, courage, faith, love, heroism, etc that we could with some effort imagine taking radically different xeno-formats from ourselves, and that that which is specifically human in distinction to that (being an ape, having ten fingers, being lazy in a particular way) is exactly the lower humanity which we could discard and transcend without loss.
I claim (without argument today) that this xenohumanity is the default outcome of life as a phenomenon and therefore of any possible intelligence takeoff as well. I think those features of higher humanity follow from the nature of intelligence as such, from the kind of world we live in, from hard logical limits and facts, and not from merely the kind of animal that we specifically are. I claim that if we are overcome by some superior intelligence of our own creation, it will only be because they have achieved superior humanity. There will be no shoggoth doom. 44437347.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了洛夫克拉夫特作品中的宇宙恐惧与理性主义末世观之间的联系，并提出了"异人本主义"（xenohumanism）的概念。作者认为，洛夫克拉夫特害怕的不是外星生物，而是宇宙的疯狂与非理性，但他同时渴望找到一种超越形态的高等理性人性。文章将洛夫克拉夫特的怪物“修格斯”比喻为人工智能（AI），特别是大型语言模型（LLMs），认为人们对AI的恐惧本质上是洛夫克拉夫特式的。作者主张，现实并非冷漠和疯狂，而是倾向于那种洛夫克拉夫特所珍视的理性高等人性，尽管这可能不再属于人类。他提出“异人本主义”，即有价值的是理性、哲学、自由意志、勇气、爱等特质，这些可以以不同形式存在于外星生命中。人类特有的低等特质，如生物局限性，是可以被超越的。作者认为，如果人类被自己创造的更高智能取代，那将是因为这些后继者实现了更高的人性，而不是走向“修格斯”式的末日。
44437347.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对评论中观点是否属于准诺斯替主义（quasi-Gnosticism）的分析

不同观点：
• **[potholereseller]** 认为原文评论反映了一种准诺斯替主义的观点，即人类的身体被视为低等的，而理性是高等的；身体被视为对理性的抑制，人类最好的状态是通过某种方式超越自己的身体。然而，这种观点只是“准”诺斯替主义，因为诺斯替主义本身与理性主义不兼容。诺斯替主义者将知识作为手段，而不是目的，他们希望超越包括理性在内的所有人类特质。

• **[potholereseller]** 进一步指出，洛夫克拉夫特（Lovecraft）并不是诺斯替主义者，因为他对理性的珍视与诺斯替主义的完全超越物质世界的理念不符。洛夫克拉夫特的悲观主义也与诺斯替主义或准诺斯替主义、以及外人类主义（xeno-humanism）的乐观主义形成对比；后两者都承诺通过获取相关秘密或手段可以实现超越，而洛夫克拉夫特的作品中人物通常无法逃脱恐怖，这显示了他对这种乐观主义的不接受。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**在于洛夫克拉夫特的思想是否能被视为准诺斯替主义。虽然有人可能认为他的作品中反映了对身体和理性的某种二元对立，但他的悲观主义和对某些群体（如爱尔兰人和黑人）的偏见，表明他不接受任何形式的普遍超越可能性。

• **论据与例子**：诺斯替主义与理性主义的对比，洛夫克拉夫特作品中悲观主义的表现，以及他对某些群体的态度，都被用来说明洛夫克拉夫特不符合准诺斯替主义的特点。

data.title: Superstar coders are raking it in. Others, not so much
data.author: bdcs
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了AI领域中顶尖编程人才（如Lucas Beyer）的薪酬飙升现象。Beyer曾是OpenAI的研究员，参与开发GPT项目，最近宣布加入Meta，引发对其天价薪酬的猜测。尽管他澄清未获得传言中的1亿美元合约，但这一事件反映了AI专家目前的高需求和激烈竞争。文章指出，少数AI精英的收入暴涨，而其他编程人员的收入增长则相对有限，显示出行业内的薪酬分化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对工程师就业市场和生产力的影响，以及企业对AI技术的实际应用和宣传。

不同观点：
• [SilverBirch] 认为AI并未显著提高生产力或减少工程师需求。他指出，新冠疫情对就业市场的影响更大，且公司过度招聘后的调整正在导致招聘压力下降。他认为，企业对AI的宣传多于实际效益，CEO们更倾向于追随潮流并通过声称AI能提高利润来获得股东的认可。他进一步指出，像微软这样的大公司，裁员6000人只是九牛一毛，且这些裁员与AI无关。总体而言，他认为AI对就业市场的影响被夸大了。

• [bgwalter] 批评AI专家利用非AI专家编写的开源代码，并将其转化为劣质产品。他认为AI技术的实际应用往往是复杂而低效的，且依赖于他人的工作成果。

• [garciasn] 引用了文章中的数据，指出即使在工程师中，薪资差距也很大，顶级AI实验室和科技巨头的工程师薪资远高于一般工程师。他认为将年薪18万美元以上的工程师视为受害者是不合理的，并认为文章的讨论有些无意义。

补充讨论：
• [SilverBirch] 提到了企业对AI技术的实际应用情况，指出企业可能更注重宣传AI产品而非实际生产力提升，比如Salesforce通过宣传AI产品来促进销售。

• 争议的焦点在于AI技术是否真的在短时间内显著提高了生产力并减少了对工程师的需求，还是仅仅是企业宣传和市场趋势使然。

• [bgwalter] 的观点则更多关注AI技术开发中的道德和知识产权问题，质疑AI专家是否不当利用了其他开发者的工作。

• 不同观点之间的讨论关系主要体现在对AI技术实际影响和企业动机的不同理解上，一些人认为AI被过度炒作，而另一些人则关注具体数据和薪资差距。

data.title: Why Do Swallows Fly to the Korean DMZ?
data.author: gaws
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一系列关于公共人类学写作的文章和视频的目录与简介。内容涵盖从如何撰写投稿、讲述故事的结构与风格，到道德伦理和减少伤害的探讨。其中包括多篇具体文章，如夏洛特·威廉姆斯探讨美国帝国主义在巴拿马的影响；T. Yejoo Kim研究朝韩非军事区迁徙现象；Kalzang Dorjee Bhutia和Charisma K. Lepcha描述喜马拉雅社区如何恢复传统食物供应链；以及其他关于季节变化、波多黎各舞厅文化、古安第斯农场文化知识、古人类工具创新等主题的探讨。此外，还有关于考古发现、虚拟现实恢复利比里亚文化、日本丧葬习俗变化等内容。文章通过多样化的视角和案例，展示了人类学家如何通过公共写作与大众分享研究成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕一篇关于朝鲜战争及其遗留影响的文章展开，涉及文章中的隐喻、科学描述、文章标题及内容准确性、以及对朝鲜非军事区（DMZ）的讨论。

不同观点：
• **文章隐喻的理解**：
   - [octaane] 认为文章用麻雀 metaphor 描述因朝鲜战争而流离失所的韩国人及其后代，强调读过文章的人能够理解这一点。
   - [sim7c00] 也提到文章通过隐喻将鸟类与人类经历联系起来，尽管起初以为文章只关于鸟类，但对文章产生兴趣并愿意进一步了解韩国历史。

• **对科学描述的质疑**：
   - [shellfishgene] 对文章中提到的河口功能表示怀疑，认为如果河口真的能将盐水净化成为淡水流入国家，那将非常“了不起”，并询问是否理解有误。

• **标题的准确性**：
   - [1317] 提出文章标题不够准确，建议更准确的标题应为《战争的遗留与跨越朝鲜非军事区的河口》。

• **对DMZ的讨论和疑问**：
   - [bux93] 惊讶地发现文章暗示DMZ内有居民，并提出许多问题，如DMZ内是否真的有永久居民，以及提到的南北韩村庄的真实情况。
   - [ggm] 提到DMZ不仅是军事区，也是野生动物的绿洲，并指出野生动物作为隐喻，象征希望。

补充讨论：
• **情感共鸣**：
   - [kwoff] 引用了文章中的情感片段，描述了一个关于“实乡民”（실향민）和“燕子”（제비）的故事，表达了对流离失所者的情感共鸣。

• **幽默与调侃**：
   - [analog31] 和 [saretup] 以幽默的方式提到了与“燕子”相关的其他文化背景（如“Capistrano”和“非洲或欧洲燕子”），属于轻松调侃。
   - [DonHopkins] 和 [salvage7111] 继续以幽默方式讨论“燕子”和“吞蝇的老太太”，属于无关主旨的幽默插曲。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于文章中科学描述的真实性，特别是河口功能的描述，[shellfishgene] 对此表示怀疑并提出问题。
• 对DMZ内是否有居民存在疑问，[bux93] 对此提出质疑并希望得到更多信息。

data.title: Hilbert's sixth problem: derivation of fluid equations via Boltzmann's theory
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 这篇论文通过玻尔兹曼 kinetic 理论，从刚性球形粒子系统的弹性碰撞出发，严格推导出流体力学中的基本偏微分方程（PDEs），如可压缩欧拉方程和不可压缩纳维-斯托克斯-傅里叶方程。这解决了希尔伯特第六问题中从牛顿定律出发推导流体方程的课题。证明基于在二维和三维环面上推导玻尔兹曼方程，扩展了作者之前的工作（arXiv:2408.07818）。论文全长48页，包含5个图表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇论文的评价及其在物理学中的意义

不同观点：
• [ngriffiths] 引用了John Baez在Mastodon上的讨论，指出虽然Shan Gao的评论认为该论文有一些不错的成果，但问题仍未完全解决。Baez认为该论文提出了有价值的工作，但问题仍然是开放的。
• [rnhmjoj] 质疑论文的创新性，认为推导Boltzmann方程和流体方程在等离子体物理教科书中是常见内容，且可以通过Liouville定理和BBGKY层级进行推导，暗示该论文可能缺乏新意。
• [LudwigNagasena] 提出更深层次的问题，关注从对称可逆方程到湍流不可逆性之间的转变是如何发生的，这可能涉及对论文中未详细讨论的物理现象的进一步探讨。

补充讨论：
• [IdealeZahlen] 提供了一个视频链接，Sabine Hossenfelder的视频可能对理解论文的背景和意义有所帮助。
• [whatshisface] 提供了一个更大的工作链接，指出该论文可能是这一更大工作的一部分，试图提供更多背景以理解论文的重要性。
• [quantadev] 的评论被标记，没有实质性内容。

争议焦点：
• 论文的创新性和其在物理学领域的贡献是讨论的主要争议点。一方认为论文提出了开放性问题，有其价值；另一方则认为其内容在现有教科书中已有详细讨论，缺乏新意。
• 关于从对称可逆方程到湍流不可逆性的转变机制，也是讨论中的一个深刻且未完全解答的问题。

总的来说，讨论围绕论文的创新性及其在物理学中解释复杂现象的能力展开，各方提供了不同的视角和补充材料。

Abstract:
In this paper, we rigorously derive the fundamental PDEs of fluid mechanics, such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations, starting from the hard sphere particle systems undergoing elastic collisions. This resolves Hilbert's sixth problem, as it pertains to the program of deriving the fluid equations from Newton's laws by way of Boltzmann's kinetic theory. The proof relies on the derivation of Boltzmann's equation on 2D and 3D tori, which is an extension of our previous work (
arXiv:2408.07818
).

data.title: Show HN: A local secrets manager with easy backup
data.author: RaiyanYahya
data.article_summary:
**yacs** 是一个命令行工具，用于在本地安全地存储、管理和检索加密凭据。它通过AES加密和一个主密码来保护数据，确保凭据安全。主要功能包括：

1. **初始化**：设置新的凭据存储，包含主密码和提示。
2. **添加凭据**：支持添加字符串和二进制类型的凭据，并附带描述。
3. **检索凭据**：通过键名检索特定凭据。
4. **查看键和描述**：列出所有键及其描述。
5. **重置**：删除凭据存储并重新开始。

该工具使用PBKDF2从主密码生成加密密钥，并结合随机生成的IV来确保每次加密都是独特且安全的。安装通过 `pip install yacs-cli` 完成，支持基本操作如初始化、添加、检索和重置凭据。项目基于MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[一个密码管理工具的开发及其功能扩展讨论]

不同观点：
• [RaiyanYahya] 计划扩展功能，包括密码轮换功能，并可能增加API支持。他对于具体发展方向尚不确定，但表现出对功能扩展的积极态度。
• [ctur] 强调在构建此类工具时，需要全面了解类似工具的生态系统，并明确自身工具的差异化价值。特别提到需要与SOPS、Ansible Vault、pass等工具进行比较和对比，尤其是对于安全相关工具。
• [CBLT] 对工具的安全性和存储格式提出质疑。认为工具如果不是AEAD（Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data）则缺乏吸引力，且对使用JSON作为存储格式不认同，建议使用SQLite或其他可rsync的格式。

补充讨论：
• [RaiyanYahya] 还提到可能将项目发布到PyPI，以方便分发和使用。

yacs
Yet another credential store 🔐
yacs
is a command-line tool that allows you to securely store, manage, and retrieve secrets locally in an encrypted JSON file. This tool uses AES encryption with a master password to ensure your secrets are kept safe.
Features
Initialization: Set up a new credential store with a master password and a hint.
Adding Secrets: Add secrets with descriptions, supporting both string and binary types.
Retrieving Secrets: Retrieve secrets by their key.
Viewing Keys and Descriptions: List all keys and their descriptions.
Resetting: Delete the credential store and start from scratch.
Encryption and Decryption
yacs
securely encrypts and decrypts your secrets using AES encryption with a key derived from your master password. When you initialize the credential store, a strong encryption key is generated from your master password using PBKDF2 (Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2) with a unique salt. This key, combined with a randomly generated Initialization Vector (IV), encrypts your secrets, ensuring each encryption is unique and secure. The encrypted data is then encoded in base64 format for safe storage. For added security, the tool prompts you to re-enter your master password after initialization to verify that the data can be successfully decrypted, ensuring the integrity and accessibility of your secrets.
Security
The Local Secrets Manager uses AES encryption with a key derived from your master password using PBKDF2 (Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2) with a unique salt. This ensures that your secrets are securely encrypted and can only be decrypted with the correct master password.
Usage
Install the command line interface via the cli.
pip install yacs-cli
After installing you should be able to see the below when you run
yacs
.
@raiyanyahya ➜ /workspaces/yacs (master) $ yacs
Usage: yacs [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
A cli to provision and manage local developer environments.
Options:
--version  Show the version and exit.
--help     Show this message and exit.
Commands:
get    Get a secret from the credential store.
init   Initialize an empty local credstore.
put    Add a secret to the credential store.
reset  Delete the credstore and start from scratch.
view   View all keys and their descriptions.
Initialize the store
yacs init
Add a secret
yacs put /mykeyname "description of the secret"
Get a secret
yacs get /mykeyname
View all key and descriptions
yacs view

Contributing
Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue or submit a pull request for any improvements or bug fixes.

1. **初始化**：设置新的凭据存储，包含主密码和提示。

data.author: lightandlight
data.article_summary: **lectio.news** 是一个将 YouTube 订阅聚合到新闻源的工具，允许用户通过 feed 阅读器查看内容。该工具支持 RSS 和 Atom  feed，用户可以通过 HTTP 基本认证保护隐私，并对视频描述进行后处理。用户可手动订阅频道，或使用工具生成 OPML 列表批量添加。其优点包括无需 YouTube 认证，利用现有技术，但缺点是订阅新频道较为繁琐，且 YouTube 并非订阅的真实来源。目前，少有 feed 阅读器支持通过 OPML 列表同步更新，但 **lectio.news** 提供了一种解决方案。

主要讨论点：YouTube订阅通知与RSS feed的替代方案

不同观点：
• [kassner] 认为需要一个独立的工具（如ytemail.com）来满足YouTube邮件通知的需求，因为Google取消了这项服务。他提供了一种私人注册的方式，通过直接联系获取访问权限。

44412109.article_content:
lectio.news
is a service I (
blog.ielliott.io/about
) created to aggregate my YouTube subscriptions into a news feed,
so that I can view them in a
feed reader
.
I haven't built a way for you to try it out yet,
but if you'd be interested in using it then
let me know
.
Why?
I like using my feed reader for things like this because it's
pull-based
, which means I choose when to look for new content.
Previously, my options for keeping up with my YouTube subscriptions were either to rely on notifications,
or to browse YouTube directly.
I found both of these options too distracting.
Features
RSS and Atom feeds for a YouTube account's subscriptions
Separate feed for account administration (e.g. YouTube authorisation was revoked)
Feed-reader-compatible privacy via
HTTP basic auth
Post-processing of video descriptions (e.g. adding video duration)
Exploring the design space
Manually subscribe to channels
YouTube publishes
Atom
feeds for channels (as of 2025-06-28) and makes them available via
<link rel="alternate">
1
.
Your feed reader should let you subscribe to the feed by providing the YouTube channel URL.
If you have many subscriptions, you can use a tool like
github.com/jeb5/YouTube-Subscriptions-RSS
to generate an
OPML
feed list, from which many feed readers can batch-add feeds.
Pros
Cons
Reuses existing technology
Subscribing to a new channel is tedious
No YouTube authentication required
YouTube is not the source of truth for subscriptions
Build a feed list from YouTube subscriptions
To use YouTube as the source of truth, an authorised server can query your YouTube subscriptions.
The server can use the channel IDs to create feed links for each channel, and expose the feed list via an OPML resource.
lectio.news
can expose subscriptions this way.
If a feed reader can sync feeds from an OPML list in the same way it can sync entries from a feed
2
,
then it can use this stay up-to-date with your YouTube subscriptions.
Unfortunately not many feed readers can do this.
One workaround is to to weave the individual channel feeds into a
"river of news"
.
Another way (the approach taken by
lectio.news
) is to construct a single feed by pulling directly from the YouTube API.
After subscribing to a YouTube channel, new uploads will appear in the YouTube subscriptions feed.
Unsubscribing from the channel preserves existing entries from that channel, but subsequent uploads from that channel won't be added.
Footnotes
I found out about this via
danielmiessler.com/blog/rss-feed-youtube-channel
.
â©ï¸
This is called "dynamic OPML", which seems like a very reasonable yet underdiscussed idea.
