44441855.article_content:
Spain and Brazil push global action to tax the super-rich and curb inequality
1 July 2025
Economic Development
Spain and Brazil have launched a joint initiative to promote higher tax contributions from the super-rich worldwide, aimed at tackling soaring inequality by ensuring those with the most pay their fair share.
Presented during the UN’s
4th International Conference on Financing for Development
– taking place this week in Sevilla, Spain – the proposal highlights a growing problem: the richest individuals often contribute less to public finances than ordinary taxpayers, thanks to lower effective tax rates and legal loopholes.
“Our countries need more and more public revenues to meet their needs. Inequality is a problem everywhere and
the richest pay less than the middle class – even less than lower-income taxpayers
,” said Spain’s Secretary of State for Finance Jesús Gascón, during a press conference at the conference venue, where temperatures have soared to record highs in recent days.
The two governments are calling on others to join a drive for a fairer, more progressive global tax system. They point to a stark reality: the wealthiest one per cent of the global population owns more than 95 per cent of humanity combined.
UN News/Matt Wells
The Spanish Secretary of State for Finance Jesús Gascón (on screen) addresses a meeting at the Financing for Development conference in Sevilla, Spain.
Sharing knowledge, closing gaps
In today’s interconnected world access to reliable data is essential. The initiative prioritises information sharing - between governments and tax authorities – to help expose gaps in tax systems, close loopholes and combat evasion and avoidance.
Improving data quality and building national capacities for data analysis will help tax administrations identify where and how wealth is concentrated, how much is currently being paid and what needs to change.
Though some progress has already been made, the countries say much more must be done and many more countries should come on board.
“
There’s a real need to know who the beneficial owners are behind companies and legal structures used to conceal wealth
,” said Mr. Gascón. The initiative also proposes technical cooperation, training in data analytics and peer review mechanisms to strengthen national tax systems.
A global wealth registry?
Spain and Brazil are even considering steps toward a global wealth registry – acknowledging that this would take time, political will and major national efforts.
But the aim is clear: more transparency, more accountability and fairer contributions from the richest.
“
We cannot tolerate the intensity of inequality, which has been increasing in recent years
,” said Brazil’s Minister-Counsellor to the UN, José Gilberto Scandiucci denying that this was some kind of far-leftist agenda.
“
This is a moderate initiative to confront a very radical reality
.”
The proposal forms part of the
Seville Platform for Action
, which is turbocharging voluntary actions to help reach the
Sustainable Development Goals
(SDGs) – currently way off track for the 2030 deadline.
G20 highlights 'high worth' factor
It also follows the 2024 agreement by the G20 industrialised nations who met in Rio (Brazil) last year – the first international accord to commit to a joint tax agenda for high-net-worth individuals.
A three-month work plan is now being drawn up with regular meetings planned to track progress. The goal – bring more countries, international organisations and civil society on board to push forward tax reforms targeting the ultra-rich.
“If we want to effectively tax the super-rich, fight inequality and make our tax systems fairer and more progressive,
we need political will – and we need to act within our means
,” Mr. Gascón added.

data.title: They tried Made in the USA – it was too expensive for their customers
data.author: petethomas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国国内生产与进口产品之间的成本、价格和生产能力平衡，以及关税政策的影响。

不同观点：
• **Strict9**：认为只有当生产规模扩大、基础设施增加、成本下降后情况才会改善。中国具有快速扩大生产线的能力，而美国已经失去了这种能力。关税不能解决问题，小规模实验也大多会失败，消费者最终会承担成本。

• **GlibMonkeyDeath**：指出即使零售商不愿提高价格，国内商品价格仍会上涨，且消费者最终会承担关税成本。以沃尔玛为例，指出即使大公司也无法承受供应链成本大幅上升的压力。

• **aeonik**：提到一些国内生产实验项目，如SmarterEveryday的尝试，尽管面临挑战，但仍有一些消费者愿意购买高价商品。

• **hammock**：通过Tuft and Needle的例子，说明一些公司最初在国内生产独特产品，但后来转向进口以降低成本，失去独特性。

• **PaulHoule**：回顾历史，指出纺织制造业早已外移，美国本土在制造业上的竞争力早已丧失。

• **rayiner**：对比1980年代与现在，指出当时国内服装生产比例高，但并未导致生活水平下降，质疑如今依赖国外廉价商品是否真正有利。

• **xiphias2**：认为美国过度依赖中国进口是不明智的地缘政治决策，应在多国间保持平衡。

• **giantg2**：质疑以昂贵的利基产品为例是否具有代表性，希望看到更多普遍商品的例子。

• **MangoToupe**：认为资本主义市场应自行解决问题，没有必要特别支持美国制造，消费者应根据市场选择产品。

• **thotghig5896**：指出低价进口商品降低了消费品价格，虽然导致美国经济依赖他国，但限制进口会导致经济困境。

• **k__**：认为美国难以在价格上竞争，但可以通过创新和新解决方案在某些领域取得优势。

• **netfl0**：不支持国内生产低端产品如塑料狗床。

• **fnordpiglet**：回顾制造业外流历史，指出美国自身生产质量下降也是原因之一，全球化只是加速了这一趋势。建议美国应发挥自身优势，而非试图恢复过去。

• **superultra**：质疑是否应在国内恢复重工业生产，指出工业劳动对环境和工人健康的长期负面影响。

• **v5v3**：建议不必所有产品都国内生产，可以仅在国内生产高端产品线，以满足不同消费群体的需求。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于是否应通过关税和国内生产来保护和促进美国制造业，以及消费者是否应为高价国内产品买单。
- 历史背景和全球化对美国制造业的影响被多次提及，尤其是生产能力和质量的变化。
- 讨论中涉及到国内生产的环境和健康代价，以及市场机制在解决这些问题中的作用。

data.title: Cloudflare to introduce pay-per-crawl for AI bots
data.author: scotchmi_st
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为“按爬取付费”（Pay per Crawl）的新方案，旨在让内容创作者对人工智能爬虫访问其内容有更多控制权。当前，内容创作者面临两个选择：完全开放或完全封锁内容访问。然而，许多出版商和内容创作者希望能通过让AI爬虫付费来获取内容访问权限。Cloudflare推出的“按爬取付费”功能允许内容所有者设置统一的收费标准，决定是否允许、收费或阻止特定爬虫访问。该系统利用HTTP 402状态码和Web Bot Auth技术确保安全和验证，同时让出版商在现有安全策略基础上灵活控制访问权限和定价。该功能目前处于私人测试阶段。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 提出的通过支付进行网页爬取的方案及其争议

不同观点：
• **支持支付爬取的立场**（asim）：asim 认为 Cloudflare 的方案为微支付提供了一种解决方案，类似于 Coinbase 引入的 x402 库。该立场支持通过支付来减少爬虫对网站的负担，并提供了一种可能的实现方式。

• **批评与替代方案建议**（JimDabell）：JimDabell 认为 Cloudflare 的方案没有为额外成本提供价值，只是简单要求支付。他建议通过共享基础设施来减少重复爬取，并认为应该有一个协作的爬虫系统，而非各自独立爬取。他还指出，支付机制未必能有效解决问题。

• **进一步改进建议**（asimpletune）：asimpletune 支持支付爬取的方向，但认为应该根据用途收费，比如研究用途可免费，商业用途则应高收费。他提出理想的世界图书馆模式，但也承认目前不可行。

• **垄断与商业利益考虑**（mattlondon）：mattlondon 认为 Google 等大公司已经通过流量交换获得了爬取的优势，而其他公司爬取内容则没有回报。因此，Cloudflare 的方案对小公司和内容所有者有利，并可能增加其客户群。

• **广泛应用的潜力**（vasilzhigilei）：vasilzhigilei 认为 Cloudflare 的方案具有巨大潜力，尤其是如果扩展到所有客户。博客所有者等可能从中受益。

• **去中心化的担忧**（Zenul_Abidin）：Zenul_Abidin 认为应该考虑去中心化的支付方案，如Chromium曾提出的Web Monetization API，以避免依赖单一供应商。

• **对互联网未来的担忧**（skenderbeu, nottorp）：skenderbeu 担心付费浏览的趋势会导致互联网封闭，nottorp 则质疑 Cloudflare 未来是否会像过去的公司一样变得普遍不受欢迎。

• **竞争影响的顾虑**（Toritori12, saddlerustle）：Toritori12 认为大公司如Google可能不受此方案影响，从而继续免费爬取。saddlerustle 则建议开发一个开放协议来处理爬取权限和支付问题，而非依赖 Cloudflare。

• **技术和道德考量**（1dom, adjfasn47573）：1dom 认为 Cloudflare 的方案会强化其在互联网中的地位，不利于去中心化和自托管。adjfasn47573 则认为互联网的变革不可避免，AI可能带来更少广告和更多真实信息的未来。

• **特殊用途的考虑**（FloatArtifact）：FloatArtifact 提出对于使用AI爬虫作为无障碍工具的用户，应该有特殊考虑，以避免验证机制带来的不便。

补充讨论：
• **支付爬取的实际操作性**：讨论中多次提到如何有效实施支付爬取，包括如何定价、如何避免小网站失去流量、以及如何处理大公司的垄断问题。
• **去中心化与开放协议的需求**：多个评论提到需要一个去中心化和开放的协议来处理爬取和支付问题，以避免依赖单一供应商。
• **互联网变革的不可避免性**：有评论认为互联网的变革是必然的，AI可能带来积极的变化。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare 方案的实际效果和公平性，尤其是对大公司和小网站的不同影响。
• 去中心化与供应商依赖的问题。
• 支付爬取是否会带来互联网的封闭和不公平竞争。

44432385.article_content:
Introducing pay per crawl: enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers for access
2025-07-01
Will Allen
Simon Newton
5 min read
A changing landscape of consumptionÂ
Many publishers, content creators and website owners currently feel like they have a binary choice â either leave the front door wide open for AI to consume everything they create, or create their own walled garden. But what if there was another way?
At Cloudflare, we started from a simple principle: we wanted content creators to have control over who accesses their work. If a creator wants to block all AI crawlers from their content, they should be able to do so. If a creator wants to allow some or all AI crawlers full access to their content for free, they should be able to do that, too. Creators should be in the driverâs seat.
After hundreds of conversations with news organizations, publishers, and large-scale social media platforms, we heard a consistent desire for a third path: Theyâd like to allow AI crawlers to access their content, but theyâd like to get compensated. Currently, that requires knowing the right individual and striking a one-off deal, which is an insurmountable challenge if you donât have scale and leverage.Â
What if I could charge a crawler?Â
We believe your choice need not be binary â there should be a third, more nuanced option:
You can charge for access.
Instead of a blanket block or uncompensated open access, we want to empower content owners to monetize their content at Internet scale.
Weâre excited to help dust off a mostly forgotten piece of the web:
HTTP response code 402
.
Introducing pay per crawl
Pay per crawl
, in private beta, is our first experiment in this area.Â
Pay per crawl integrates with existing web infrastructure, leveraging HTTP status codes and established authentication mechanisms to create a framework for paid content access.Â
Each time an AI crawler requests content, they either present payment intent via request headers for successful access (
HTTP response code 200
), or receive a
402 Payment Required
response with pricing. Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record for pay per crawl and also provides the underlying technical infrastructure.
Publisher controls and pricing
Pay per crawl grants domain owners full control over their monetization strategy. They can define a flat, per-request price across their entire site. Publishers will then have three distinct options for a crawler:
Allow:
Grant the crawler free access to content.
Charge:
Require payment at the configured, domain-wide price.
Block:
Deny access entirely, with no option to pay.
An important mechanism here is that even if a crawler doesnât have a billing relationship with Cloudflare, and thus couldnât be charged for access, a publisher can still choose to âchargeâ them. This is the functional equivalent of a network level block (an HTTP
403 Forbidden
response where no content is returned) â but with the added benefit of telling the crawler there could be a relationship in the future.Â
While publishers currently can define a flat price across their entire site, they retain the flexibility to bypass charges for specific crawlers as needed. This is particularly helpful if you want to allow a certain crawler through for free, or if you want to negotiate and execute a content partnership outside the pay per crawl feature.Â
To ensure integration with each publisherâs existing security posture, Cloudflare enforces Allow or Charge decisions via a rules engine that operates only after existing WAF policies and bot management or bot blocking features have been applied.
Payment headers and access
As we were building the system, we knew we had to solve an incredibly important technical challenge: ensuring we could charge a specific crawler, but prevent anyone from spoofing that crawler. Thankfully, thereâs a way to do this using
Web Bot Auth
proposals.
For crawlers,
this involves:
Generating an Ed25519 key pair, and making the
JWK
-formatted public key available in a hosted directory
Registering with Cloudflare to provide the URL of your key directory and user agent information.
Configuring your crawler to use
HTTP Message Signatures
with each request.
Once registration is accepted, crawler requests should always include
signature-agent
,
signature-input
, and
signature
headers to identify your crawler and discover paid resources.

44432385.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为“按爬取付费”（Pay per Crawl）的新方案，旨在让内容创作者对人工智能爬虫访问其内容有更多控制权。当前，内容创作者面临两个选择：完全开放或完全封锁内容访问。然而，许多出版商和内容创作者希望能通过让AI爬虫付费来获取内容访问权限。Cloudflare推出的“按爬取付费”功能允许内容所有者设置统一的收费标准，决定是否允许、收费或阻止特定爬虫访问。该系统利用HTTP 402状态码和Web Bot Auth技术确保安全和验证，同时让出版商在现有安全策略基础上灵活控制访问权限和定价。该功能目前处于私人测试阶段。
44432385.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare 提出的通过支付进行网页爬取的方案及其争议

不同观点：
• **支持支付爬取的立场**（asim）：asim 认为 Cloudflare 的方案为微支付提供了一种解决方案，类似于 Coinbase 引入的 x402 库。该立场支持通过支付来减少爬虫对网站的负担，并提供了一种可能的实现方式。

• **批评与替代方案建议**（JimDabell）：JimDabell 认为 Cloudflare 的方案没有为额外成本提供价值，只是简单要求支付。他建议通过共享基础设施来减少重复爬取，并认为应该有一个协作的爬虫系统，而非各自独立爬取。他还指出，支付机制未必能有效解决问题。

• **进一步改进建议**（asimpletune）：asimpletune 支持支付爬取的方向，但认为应该根据用途收费，比如研究用途可免费，商业用途则应高收费。他提出理想的世界图书馆模式，但也承认目前不可行。

• **垄断与商业利益考虑**（mattlondon）：mattlondon 认为 Google 等大公司已经通过流量交换获得了爬取的优势，而其他公司爬取内容则没有回报。因此，Cloudflare 的方案对小公司和内容所有者有利，并可能增加其客户群。

• **广泛应用的潜力**（vasilzhigilei）：vasilzhigilei 认为 Cloudflare 的方案具有巨大潜力，尤其是如果扩展到所有客户。博客所有者等可能从中受益。

• **去中心化的担忧**（Zenul_Abidin）：Zenul_Abidin 认为应该考虑去中心化的支付方案，如Chromium曾提出的Web Monetization API，以避免依赖单一供应商。

• **对互联网未来的担忧**（skenderbeu, nottorp）：skenderbeu 担心付费浏览的趋势会导致互联网封闭，nottorp 则质疑 Cloudflare 未来是否会像过去的公司一样变得普遍不受欢迎。

• **竞争影响的顾虑**（Toritori12, saddlerustle）：Toritori12 认为大公司如Google可能不受此方案影响，从而继续免费爬取。saddlerustle 则建议开发一个开放协议来处理爬取权限和支付问题，而非依赖 Cloudflare。

• **技术和道德考量**（1dom, adjfasn47573）：1dom 认为 Cloudflare 的方案会强化其在互联网中的地位，不利于去中心化和自托管。adjfasn47573 则认为互联网的变革不可避免，AI可能带来更少广告和更多真实信息的未来。

• **特殊用途的考虑**（FloatArtifact）：FloatArtifact 提出对于使用AI爬虫作为无障碍工具的用户，应该有特殊考虑，以避免验证机制带来的不便。

补充讨论：
• **支付爬取的实际操作性**：讨论中多次提到如何有效实施支付爬取，包括如何定价、如何避免小网站失去流量、以及如何处理大公司的垄断问题。
• **去中心化与开放协议的需求**：多个评论提到需要一个去中心化和开放的协议来处理爬取和支付问题，以避免依赖单一供应商。
• **互联网变革的不可避免性**：有评论认为互联网的变革是必然的，AI可能带来积极的变化。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare 方案的实际效果和公平性，尤其是对大公司和小网站的不同影响。
• 去中心化与供应商依赖的问题。
• 支付爬取是否会带来互联网的封闭和不公平竞争。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者对收集到的数千个益智药（nootropics）评分的分析。益智药广义上指任何声称能提升认知能力的物质，包括处方药、植物、少量娱乐药物以及像睡眠和锻炼等活动。由于个体差异，益智药的效果因人而异。作者开发了一个推荐系统，用户输入自己尝试过的益智药评分，系统会推荐可能适合他们的其他益智药。作者收集了1981人的29,387个评分，加上之前的数据共36,163个评分。评分采用0-10的尺度，0代表完全无效或副作用过大，1-4代表可能有效果，5-9代表明显效果，10代表改变生活。分析中考虑了缺乏随机分配、自我报告偏差和缺乏控制与盲法等偏见。这些评分帮助预测某个人对特定益智药的潜在反应，但需注意结果可能受到 placebo 效应的影响。所有数据和代码均公开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：有关益智药（nootropics）的有效性和安全性讨论

不同观点：
• **益智药与自然活动的对比**：
   - **negativepanda**：认为简单的益智药如咖啡加上自然散步比单独做一件事效果更好，且这种组合能带来期待感。
   - **reverendsteveii**：通过每天20分钟的阻力训练和有氧运动，得到了显著的益智效果，并认为运动是改变生活的“益智药”。

• **益智药效果的持久性与副作用**：
   - **icameron**：基于个人经验，认为益智药在初期效果明显，但随着时间推移，大脑会适应，效果减弱，甚至可能产生副作用，最终适得其反。例如SNRIs和Kratom都出现了类似的问题。
   - **butlike**：指出像安非他明这样的药物可能带来的改变未必是正面的，暗指其潜在的负面影响。

• **对益智药讨论的信任问题**：
   - **taeric**：认为由于缺乏大规模随机试验，益智药的讨论充满不确定性，尤其在自己使用Adderall的情况下，更加难以信任这些讨论。
   - **cckolon**：质疑个人经验的说服力，认为如果没有盲法试验，很难确定效果是否为安慰剂效应。

• **特定物质的讨论**：
   - **gavinray**：认为Modafinil、Racetams、Phenibut等物质效果明显，但Noopept未被提及，表示困惑。
   - **wslh**：强调某些物质如安非他明对大脑功能有直接且不可逆的影响，需给予强烈警告，与Omega-3等其他物质形成对比。

• **运动作为益智药的讨论**：
   - **Workaccount2**：强调运动的重要性，批评许多人抱怨健康问题却不愿尝试运动。
   - **Analemma_**：总结认为，除ADHD药物外，大多数益智药效果有限，而运动尤其是重量训练和高强度间歇训练（HIIT）具有显著益智效果，这符合进化视角。

补充讨论：
• **益智药的文化与信息来源**：
   - **readthenotes1**：提到益智药社区和初学者指南，并指出一些信息中的拼写错误，反映出对益智药讨论中的信息质量问题。

• **外部资源与数据支持**：
   - **runamuck**：提到Scott Alexander的益智药调查和分析，提供了一个外部资源以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 益智药的长期效果与副作用：个人经验显示益智药初期有效，但随着时间推移效果减弱并可能产生副作用，这与运动等自然方式的持久效果形成对比。
• 对益智药讨论的信任度：缺乏大规模试验导致对益智药效果的信任问题，尤其是在涉及药物如Adderall的情况下。

总结：评论围绕益智药的有效性、副作用、自然活动的替代效果以及对益智药讨论的信任问题展开，强调了运动作为一种有效的益智方式，并对某些药物的长期效果和潜在风险提出了警告。

Home
About

What I learned gathering thousands of nootropic ratings
March 23, 2022
tags:
nootropics
,
data-analysis
Credit: Ultra Heaven
In this post, I analyze nootropics ratings I gathered through a
recommender system
. Jump directly to
What I learned
if you don’t like caveats and methodology.
INTRODUCTION
#
What is a nootropic?
I will use the term
nootropic
as broadly as possible to describe
“Any substance purported to increase or enhance cognitive abilities."
Some only use the term
nootropic
to refer to a specific thing which should check a
very specific checklist
, e.g. having very few side-effects. As I’m not using this definition,
remember that the
nootropics
mentioned here can be very dangerous
.
This includes prescribed medications, plants, recreational drugs in small quantities, and more (I even included activities like sleep or exercise). If you hadn’t heard of “nootropics” before, you should also know that some people like to experiment with them and share their experience on communities like the
nootropics subreddit
, which has a great
begginer’s guide
.
The effectiveness of a nootropic varies a lot from one person to another (
your mileage will vary
). This is why I built a
nootropic recommendation system
Enter ratings on nootropics you’ve tried, and it will spit out nootropics liked by people with similar rating patterns. This was initially based on the
2016 SlateStarCodex nootropics survey
data.
, which I suggest you try before reading this post.
Still, it is helpful to understand how good each nootropic is in general, if only to prioritize further research. Indeed, my cunning plan with this recommendation system was to incentivize people to answer a boring survey. My plan worked better than I expected, and I got 1981 people to enter 29,387 nootropic ratings
Adding to it the original SlateStarCodex data, we have 36,163 ratings from 2,802 people.
, which I analyse in this post. Thanks everybody!
All data and code can be found
here
.
RATINGS
#
People interested in the code or the details of the analysis can look at
the RMarkdown notebook
.
How to interpret these ratings
#
Scale
#
I used the scale from
SlateStarCodex nootropics surveys
, which is:
0 means a substance was totally useless, or had so many side effects you couldn’t continue taking it.
1 - 4 means subtle effects, maybe placebo but still useful.
5 - 9 means strong effects, definitely not placebo.
10 means life-changing.
Ok but why?
I mostly used this scale so I could use SSC data when launching my recommendation system, but let me try to defend it. When someone tries a nootropic, either it seems to work, and the person will continue taking it, or it doesn’t seem to work, and the person will quickly stop taking it. This means we should expect people to have more certainty about nootropics that seem to work at least a little than on nootropics that don’t seem to work. If we want to compress a user experience into a 1D number, it makes sense to allow a more fine-grained judgment on positive nootropics
Why not make a scale from -10 to 10 then? Well, I just stole the scale, you know, but I think people really hate entering fine-grained ratings when they don’t have enough information.
. An issue is that this doesn’t differentiate between “Doesn’t do anything” and “I cannot feel my left arm anymore after trying this nootropic”. I tried to remedy this by asking people about the issues they had. Another issue is that some people might not read the scale description and think below 5 is negative and above is positive. I tried to take this into account in my analysis.
Biases
#
In order of importance (I think):
Lack of random allocation
The people who entered their rating on my recommender system were not randomly assigned to try specific nootropics. Thus we can expect a (usually positive) correlation between “I’m likely to try nootropic A” and “Nootropic A might work on me”.
This means that my estimations don’t represent the ratings a random person would get on average (which would usually be lower); they’re instead a prediction of the rating that a person would give to a nootropic if they decided to take it organically. Take this into account when transferring the results to yourself.
Self-report
You take a pill. It makes you feel good. You go on a website which asks you how good the pill is. You say it’s awesome. Little did you know that it was, in fact, merely good.
Take this into account when reading these ratings, especially if improving your mood is not your main goal.
Lack of control and blinding
Relatedly, these uncontrolled and unblinded ratings are partly driven by the placebo effect.
The sophisticated objection would be that this is probably less of a problem than for normal medications. The
placebo effect seems to be in large part due to regression to the mean
(when you’re sick, you’ll likely get better with time, not worse), which should not be an issue for nootropics in most cases. But the placebo effect does seem to be r

Alberto Fortin是一位有15年经验的软件工程师，他分享了使用大型语言模型（LLM）的实际体验。最初，他对LLM充满热情，希望其能革新开发流程，但在使用Go和ClickHouse重建基础设施时遇到许多问题。他的博客和后续分析指出，AI的宣传与现实存在差距，尽管新模型如Claude Opus 4有所改进，但仍未完全解决核心问题。

Alberto强调，LLM在初期使用时看似能大幅提升生产力，但实际上在处理复杂生产代码时经常出现错误，导致开发者需要耗费更多时间修复。他建议开发者应将LLM视为辅助工具，而非主导，保持对代码库的完全掌控。最终，他呼吁理性看待AI技术，既要利用其优势，也要认识到其局限性，找到平衡的使用方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **LLMs在生成代码方面的局限性**：[x187463] 认为LLMs生成的代码缺乏开发者的认知参与，管理这些代码很困难，尤其在需要长期维护的项目中。LLMs更适合一次性脚本或短期项目。
• **LLMs可能降低生产力**：[stephendause] 指出LLMs有时会因为提供错误信息而让用户走上错误的路径，浪费时间。虽然总体上LLMs是有帮助的，但需要用户检查其来源。
• **LLMs如类固醇，效果与副作用并存**：[noisy_boy] 将LLMs比作类固醇，认为其能快速提高生产力，但副作用明显，例如编程能力的退化。
• **LLMs忽视简单而重要的设计原则**：[jimbokun] 认为LLMs容易生成复杂的、难以重构和理解的代码，而忽视了将复杂问题分解为简单组件的重要性。
• **LLMs作为代码审查和概念解释工具**：[seanw444] 和[Const-me] 都将LLMs用作个性化的、快速的知识获取工具，而不是完整的代码生成器。Const-me还提到LLMs在代码审查中的作用，尽管需要筛选其建议。

补充讨论：
• **LLMs的局限性和特定领域表现不佳**：[quaintdev] 分享了LLMs在解决特定技术问题时的不足，例如无法提供最佳解决方案。
• **LLMs是新的速成方案现象**：[andy99] 认为LLMs是一种新的快速解决方案潮流，但现实中并没有真正的捷径，只有权衡和取舍。
• **LLMs在不同工作流中的应用**：[jjice] 和[hedgehog] 都提到LLMs在减少重复性工作方面的优势，例如生成模板代码和测试。同时，他们也强调了提示词优化和代码审查的重要性。
• **LLMs信仰与实际效果的争议**：[obirunda] 指出了对LLMs效果的信仰差异，一些人认为LLMs能大幅提高生产力，而另一些人则对其效果持怀疑态度。
• **LLMs未来发展的可能性**：[kadhirvelm] 提出了LLMs作为编译器的未来可能性，认为未来可能无需直接关注代码，而只需关注功能特性。

争议焦点：
• LLMs在编程中的实际效果和长期影响：一些人认为LLMs能显著提高生产力，而另一些人则担心其副作用和对开发者能力的侵蚀。
• LLMs在生成和维护复杂代码项目中的可行性：有观点认为LLMs更适合一次性任务或简单任务，而在复杂项目中表现不佳。

44443109.article_content:
← Back to Blog
Why I'm Dialing Back My LLM Usage
Alberto Fortin
From the
Agentic Engineering Sessions
|
Aired on
July 1st, 2025
We invited
Alberto Fortin
, a seasoned software engineer with 15 years of experience, to share his candid journey with AI. Alberto initially embraced LLMs with genuine enthusiasm, hoping they would revolutionize his development workflow. However, after encountering significant challenges while rebuilding his infrastructure with Go and ClickHouse, he wrote a
thoughtful blog post
reflecting on the gap between AI hype and reality.
For this conversation, Alberto also prepared a
detailed follow-up analysis
testing newer models like Claude Opus 4, examining whether recent improvements have addressed the core issues he encountered.
His experience provides practical lessons for engineers evaluating LLMs in production environments—balancing realistic expectations with an understanding of where these tools genuinely add value versus where they still fall short.
You can
watch the session on YouTube
or read below for some selected quotes.
The Reality Check: When AI Hype Meets Production Code
"I was really shocked at the poor quality of some things, and it was not just about bugs and features not working. I think as a developer who wants to maintain this codebase for the next few years, I also care about it being neat enough."
"I feel like I'm a week away from fixing this, but actually a new small error would come up and then that will take another two weeks to fix."
"I will give my error output to the LLM and then it will spit out something new that will kind of fix it, but also make things a bit more messed up—and break something else in the process."
The Productivity Illusion
"I think everyone just got a little bit overexcited about it because the first iteration, the first little feature, the first autocomplete is like, 'Oh my God, this is amazing. This is like reading my mind.' So you kind of get duped into it a little bit."
"I think we've gotten to a level where we can do probably 10 times as much coding. So we kind of expect that to happen and we require that from the LLMs, but I think everyone just gets a little bit overexcited about it."
Taking Control: The Mental Shift
"I think this is the biggest difference, like a mental shift... I am the software engineer, the senior software engineer, I am the architect. The LLM is the assistant. The assistant responds to me; I make the plan."
"I lost all my trust in LLMs, so I wouldn't give them a big feature again. I'll do very small things like refactoring or a very small-scoped feature."
"I started fixing the bugs myself. Because as soon as you understand this—you have a hundred percent understanding of your codebase and what everything is doing—it's so much easier and quicker for you to go in and fix something."
Practical Wisdom
"If you are confident enough in your skills—you know, a senior developer—and this is not working for you, there's nothing wrong with you. Just try to do the things that you always did and use AI to leverage your knowledge a little bit."
"We've gone up a level, it's great. But also, let's be mindful we're not there yet at the next level... We are offloading some of the programming work, but we still need to do architectural abstractions and make the decisions for the product."
"Let's just try to calm down all this hype and find a balanced approach towards AI. Use it, because I think it's such an amazing revolution in technology, but we're not there yet."
Learn more about Agentic Engineering
Working toward genuine, quality software in an era where code production is not the constraint anymore. Learn our take about
Agentic Engineering
and catch up with all the sessions where we're joined by experts to further develop this topic.

data.title: Exploiting the IKKO Activebuds "AI powered" earbuds
data.author: ajdude
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者购买并研究一款运行Android系统的无线耳塞式设备的过程。该设备因其集成了ChatGPT和其他AI功能而在TikTok上走红。作者通过ADB方式破解设备，发现其直接与OpenAI的API通信，并包含一个OpenAI的密钥。设备还提供了一些应用程序，如Spotify和游戏，但由于屏幕小，操作不便。在研究过程中，作者提取了设备中的APK文件，发现了加密的API端点和密钥，并成功在一个已root的设备上运行了相关应用。此外，作者还提到设备有不同的模式，如“愤怒的Dan”和“恋爱中的Dan”，这些模式有不同的系统提示。最终，作者对该设备的安全性和功能实现提出了质疑和分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某公司处理安全漏洞的回应及其引发的广泛讨论

不同观点：
• **对公司回应的肯定**：
  - [memesarecool] 认为该公司在漏洞报告处理上比98%的公司都要好，表现出兴趣并积极解决问题。尽管初期对安全性重视不够，但公司展现了责任感。
  
• **对反常现象的讽刺与担忧**：
  - [psim1] 预测未来将有大量不成熟的AI应用进入市场，呼吁关注网络安全，并暗示现在可能是进入该行业的时机。
  - [mikeve] 讽刺帖子中将运行DOOM游戏列为首要问题，而不是客户数据被盗。
  
• **对公司行为的批评与不信任**：
  - [neya] 和 [wedn3sday] 都提到公司试图通过赞助空YouTube频道来掩盖问题，认为这是不道德的行为。
  - [aidos] 对公司声称“技术团队正在努力解决问题”表示怀疑，质疑其是否真的会 diligently 处理。

• **技术层面的讨论**：
  - [JohnMakin] 指出“decrypt”功能仅解码base64是令人难以置信的错误，并提到很多人对base64的安全性存在误解。
  - [brahyam] 分享了其在保护应用免受类似问题影响方面的经验，并提供了几个开源项目作为例子，同时指出了这些项目在滥用保护机制上的不足，进而介绍了自己的开源SDK项目。

• **幽默与娱乐视角**：
  - [ixtli] 和 [jotalea] 以幽默的口吻评论帖子内容，认为这是有趣的“运行DOOM”相关帖，甚至期待看到更多类似的娱乐内容。
  
• **对安全警告的反思**：
  - [mmaunder] 引用了系统提示中关于禁止讨论中国政治的警告，并结合自身经验反思在安全防护中使用“PEOPLE WILL DIE”这类极端警告的必要性和后果。

• **对标题和内容表达的批评**：
  - [jahsome] 批评有人在标题上做文章，结果却让标题更难理解，暗示这种编辑是多余且无效的。

补充讨论：
- **争议的焦点**在于公司对安全漏洞的处理态度和方法，部分评论赞赏公司的积极回应，另一部分则质疑其真实意图和行为。
- **技术层面的讨论**主要围绕具体漏洞的严重性和技术实现的业余性，以及如何通过开源项目提升安全性。
- **幽默评论**为讨论增添了轻松的氛围，但也有人对标题和内容的表达方式提出批评。

44443919.article_content:
So my journey with these earbuds started after I saw them on
this
Mrwhosetheboss video about pointless tech. This device seems to be also popular on TikTok. My suspicions were confirmed, this runs android. So of course i went ahead and bought them.
245 euros later... and they finally arrived!
Before we dive further into this, unlike with
rabbit
, this issue has been properly reported and patched. This is also my first real blog post/disclosure so feedback is appreciated.
Small overview
I like how they strapped a USB-c cable to the outside of the box while there is also a smaller one inside the box. They ran out of box space it seems...
I also wonder if they are legally allowed to use this OpenAI logo (probably not lol)
Anyways, we aren't here for fancy boxes, lets get to the main point. The device itself boots up to a screen with the time and ChatGPT front and center.
There are some other AI features available too like translations. But this isn't a review of the device, you can watch
other YouTube videos
about that. The ChatGPT animation looks way too similar to the actual app and OpenAI could probably get them in legal trouble for stealing their brand identity. I will also mention that the audio quality is absolute shit if you use their EQ profiles but can be upped to a usable level by tweaking the EQ curves yourself.
There are also some apps available in the IKKO store, the reason that there is no google play store available is because these apps are modified specifically for the screen on the ActiveBuds, at least, that is what the CEO says about them. We will check that out in a bit. These apps include some music apps like Spotify, but also some gaming apps like, oh god, SUBWAY SURFERS BAYBEEEEE
Of course all of them unbearable to navigate due to the small screen. However we can now confirm that it most definitely runs android.
Time for some hacking
There is sadly no browser available to directly download other apps. And while you can open the native android settings app, clicking the build number 7 times does not enable developer mode. So i couldn't enable adb it seems. Is it locked that well? heh nope.
Let's just plug it into a pc and see what happens....
What the fuck, they left ADB enabled. Well, this makes it a lot easier.
After sideloading the obligatory DOOM, i began checking out how the ChatGPT integration works on the backend. I first started HTTP inspecting the device, however since i couldn't enable the proper system certificates without rooting the device, i couldn't see exactly to what URL it communicated. Fortunately that wasn't really needed.
Holy shit, holy shit, holy shit, it communicates DIRECTLY TO OPENAI. This means that a ChatGPT key must be present on the device!
I know that this device can be rooted to get the proper certificates installed because
a tool
exists on all Spreadtrum/Unisoc devices which can be used to unlock the bootloader as long as companies use the default signing keys. This was indeed the case here too. However, i couldn't get past the confirmation screen as the device does not have a volume up key to confirm the unlock. I think you are able to sign your own partitions to make it flash them without an unlocked bootloader but that's a bit too advanced for my own liking.
So, i went back to the drawing board and just dumped all of the apps from it with an APK extractor tool. After popping the launcher app into JADX, things immediately became concerning.
The device can communicate to either of these domains.
api.openai.com
Obvious, the OpenAI API
chat1.chat.iamjoy.cn
Seems to be the API for the entire device, including features not related to ChatGPT like the app store. Loading it up in a browser gives a login page.
chat2.chat.iamjoy.cn
Same thing as chat1, possibly a backup server?
openspeech.bytedance.com
No idea, might be a speech recogniser backup instead of whisper, haven't seen communication to this from the device.
www.airdimple.cn
Seems like an OpenAI API mirror or proxy?
Knowing this i went hunting for api endpoints and keys. I found a file called SecurityStringsAPI which contained encrypted endpoints and authentication keys.
You might think, hey that's just base64 idiot, the most basic encoding known to mankind. And well, yeah, it is.
However, there is a second stage which is handled by a native library which is obfuscated to hell. I am not going to even try to read that. Fortunately i didn't have to. I just sideloaded the app on a different device which was rooted, and well,
just like the rabbit apk
, it just works!
Inspecting this device:
Yup, that's an OpenAI key.
Now, while having this access, we can also expose their (pretty funny) system prompt.
The device also has another few modes, which are Angry Dan and In-Love Dan. For the angry one you need to confirm you are 18+ because it actually swears a lot.
The system prompts for these are a bit more boring.
I also noticed that it logs the chat to another endpoint on the chat1 domain. This is probably just

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Azure角色权限过度授予和API漏洞带来的安全风险。安全研究人员发现，一些Azure内置角色被错误配置为权限过度宽泛，授予了超出预期的权限。此外，Azure API存在一个漏洞，可能导致VPN密钥泄露。这两者结合形成了一条新的攻击链，使低权限用户能够访问内部云资源和本地网络。

文章首先介绍了Azure RBAC（基于角色的访问控制）的基本概念，包括安全主体、角色定义和权限范围。Azure提供超过400个内置角色，分为通用角色和服务特定角色。通用角色易于管理但权限较宽，而服务特定角色更安全但需要更细致的管理。

研究揭示了一些角色如“Reader”和“Workbook Reader”的权限定义相对合理，但“Managed Applications Reader”等角色可能被不当利用，导致潜在安全风险。

为防范这些威胁，组织应仔细审查角色权限分配，采用最小权限原则，并及时更新安全策略。

Azure's Role Roulette: How Over-Privileged Roles and API Vulnerabilities Expose Enterprise Networks
Ariel Simon
Security Researcher
No items found.
TL;DR
Token Security researchers have discovered several Azure built-in roles that are misconfigured to be over-privileged - they grant more permissions than intended by Azure.
In addition, we discovered another vulnerability in the Azure API that allows attackers to
leak VPN keys
.
Combined, these two issues create a new attack chain that lets a
weak user gain access to both internal cloud assets and on-premises networks.
In this report, we detail the research process that led to the discoveries, their implications, and what organizations can do to stay safe against these threats and other identity-driven attacks.
What is Azure RBAC?
Before jumping in, letâs discuss some basics.
Azureâs permissions model, Azure RBAC (Role-Based Access Control), is, as the name states, based on roles.
Roles are basically groups of permissions that can be assigned to principals (users, service principals, groups, etc). When granting a role to a principal, you create a
role assignment
.
â
Every
role assignment
contains three main components:
Security Principal
- Who is given the permissions?
Role Definition
- Which role is assigned? What permissions does it grant? This section states the name of the role and the
Actions
and
Not Actions
(allow or deny) that this role is granting.
Scope
- What resources is the principal given access to? The scope can be vast, such as an entire management group or subscription, or more specific, like a resource group or a single resource (e.g., a specific VM or storage account).
Role assignment
Azure roles
In Azure, there are more than 400 built-in roles, which can be divided into 2 categories:
Generic
- Roles that grant permissions that apply across all resources and all Azure services in the given scope (e.g.,
Contributor
,
Owner
,
Reader
,
etc.
)
Service-specific
- Roles that grant permissions for a specific service or function in the given scope (e.g.,
Storage Blob Data Reader
or
Virtual Machine Contributor
).
If you assign the
Contributor
role over a subscription scope, it will grant permissions to perform actions over all of the resources in this subscription, regardless if theyâre storage accounts, virtual machines, or any other resource. But if you assign the
Virtual Machine Contributor
, it will grant these permissions only to perform actions over virtual machines in the subscription.
So we can see the tradeoff here: using service-specific roles is the more secure approach, since you are granting fewer permissions, but the generic roles are easier to use since you need to manage fewer roles assignments.
The Problem
Letâs take a look at few roles and their permissions. See if you can tell where things go wrong.
The Reader role
One of Azureâs built-in roles, called
Reader,
is a generic role. As youâd expect, it gives read-only permissions over the resources in the chosen scope. Letâs examine its
role definition
:
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "View all resources, but does not allow you to make any changes.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"name": "acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"*/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Reader role definition
As we can see in the
actions
property, the permission given is
*/read
, which means it lets you perform any read action in the given scope.
*Note that this does not include data actions (reading data objects like files in storage accounts, key vault secrets, etc). Those require different, service-specific sensitive permissions.
Okay, so a generic role giving generic read permissions, that makes sense.
What about the permissions of service-specific roles?
Workbook Reader
{
"assignableScopes": [
"/"
],
"description": "Can read workbooks.",
"id": "/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"name": "b279062a-9be3-42a0-92ae-8b3cf002ec4d",
"permissions": [
{
"actions": [
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooks/revisions/read",
"microsoft.insights/workbooktemplates/read"
],
"notActions": [],
"dataActions": [],
"notDataActions": []
}
],
"roleName": "Workbook Reader",
"roleType": "BuiltInRole",
"type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions"
}
Workbook Reader role definition
If we analyze the
actions
property, we can see that as the description states, it grants read permissions to a few workbook-related objects. So a service-specific role that grants access to a specific service! So far so good.

Now, letâs check the
Managed Applications Reader
role, which its description is
âLets you read resources in a managed app

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的自动调整robots.txt功能及其对AI爬虫和网站流量的影响

不同观点：
• [jasonthorsness] 提到该功能会自动调整robots.txt，但不清楚具体还做了什么，表达了对功能透明度的关注。
• [Meekro] 认为使用Cloudflare的基本缓存配置应能处理爬虫流量，不理解为何人们对此感到困扰，尤其是考虑到当前带宽和CPU成本较低。
• [postalcoder] 指出该功能会阻止遵守robots.txt的透明AI爬虫，这可能反而激励这些爬虫隐藏自己。同时也引用链接说明隐藏行为并不有效。
• [dirkc] 怀疑通过阻止爬虫是否能有效保护原创内容不被用于LLM训练，认为内容最终可能会进入某些LLM的训练集。
• [NullCascade] 提出相反的问题，如何优化内容使其更可能被AI爬虫抓取，指出传统SEO可能不够。
• [btown] 指出该功能是选择性加入的，而非默认开启，同时提到Cloudflare的权力问题。
• [blakesterz] 提到目前被阻止的爬虫列表很短。
• [Sol-] 质疑主要AI公司是否真正遵守robots.txt，怀疑他们有隐藏的爬取行为。
• [account42] 担心此功能会导致普通用户遇到更多CAPTCHA验证。
• [dawnerd] 分享了个人经验，表示该功能有效减少了服务器负载，特别提到了对微软和Meta流量的阻止效果。
• [alganet] 认为AI自由使用网站数据会导致人们失去创造数字内容的动力，预测AI会最终摧毁网络。
• [badlibrarian] 询问是否修复了自动阻止RSS feed的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对Cloudflare功能的实际效果、透明度、以及对AI公司遵守规则的信任问题。
• 有人关注该功能对普通用户体验的影响，如[account42]提到的CAPTCHA问题。
• 讨论中还提到了具体技术实现和配置细节，如[dawnerd]分享的实际配置经验和效果。
• 链接和引用提供了额外的背景信息和深入讨论，如[postalcoder]和[cmg]提供的链接。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于该功能是否有效保护网站内容以及其对不同类型流量的处理方式，特别是对AI爬虫的阻止是否会产生反效果，以及对普通用户体验的影响。

data.title: Private sector lost 33k jobs, badly missing expectations of 100k increase
data.author: ceejayoz
data.article_summary: 2023年6月，私营部门招聘意外收缩，ADP报告显示私营部门减少了33,000个工作岗位，为2023年3月以来首次下降。经济学家此前预计增加100,000个岗位。服务业岗位受创最重，专业/商业服务和医疗/教育领域分别减少了56,000和52,000个岗位。尽管制造业和采矿业岗位增加，整体服务岗位减少了66,000个。中西部和西部地区就业收缩最严重，而南部地区岗位增加。小型企业岗位流失最多，而拥有超过500名员工的大型企业岗位增长最多。工资增长略有放缓，S&P 500指数今年上涨超过4%。经济不确定性增加，投资者正密切关注即将发布的政府就业报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对就业市场和经济健康的分析及对ADP报告的评价

不同观点：
• psunavy03认为，目前的失业率指标不够全面，无法反映人们是否能够通过工作维持稳定生活。他指出，失业率没有包括那些没有积极找工作的人，且低薪工作与高薪工作对经济的贡献不同。
• JumpCrisscross提供了ADP报告的具体数据，指出商品生产公司就业增加，而服务行业就业减少，且不同地区和公司规模的就业变化不一。
• issafram表示，自己以前经常收到很多招聘信息，但最近几个月明显减少，对就业市场变化并不感到意外。
• hliyan提醒，ADP报告在预测政府就业报告方面的记录并不稳定，暗示其可靠性可能有限。
• giantg2表示自己即将失去工作，认为就业市场状况很糟糕。
• jimbokun质疑关税政策是否是导致商品生产岗位增加而服务岗位减少的原因。
• quantum_state认为，政府的关税政策正在损害消费者，并预测会有更多坏消息。
• analyte123批评ADP报告的局限性，指出其数据仅基于使用ADP支付服务的公司，可能不具代表性。
• programmertote分享了自己所在公司因房地产市场的潜在风险而裁员的情况。
• bix6和underlipton则以较为调侃的语气讨论了未来可能的利率削减和数据修正。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对ADP报告的可靠性和代表性存在争议，部分评论者如JumpCrisscross和analyte123对其数据和结论持不同程度的怀疑态度。
• 评论中还涉及对关税政策的讨论，jimbokun和quantum_state认为关税政策对就业市场有负面影响。
• 个人经历和具体数据在讨论中都被用作支持各自观点的论据，如psunavy03的生活质量论据和programmertote的裁员实例。
• 部分评论带有明显的政治色彩，如dyauspitr对政府的批评，显示出就业问题在政治语境下的敏感性。

Key Points
Private sector hiring unexpectedly contracted in June, payrolls processing firm ADP said Wednesday.
It's a potential sign that the economy may not be as sturdy as investors believe.
People visit booths set up by the City of Sunrise and their police department at the Mega JobNewsUSA South Florida Job Fair at the Amerant Bank Arena on April 30, 2025 in Sunrise, Florida.
Joe Raedle | Getty Images
Private sector hiring unexpectedly contracted in June, payrolls processing firm ADP said Wednesday, in a possible sign that the economy may not be as sturdy as investors believe as they bid the
S&P 500
back up to record territory to end the month.
Private payrolls lost 33,000 jobs in June, the ADP report showed, the first decrease since March 2023. Economists polled by Dow Jones forecast an increase of 100,000 for the month. The May job growth figure was revised even lower to just 29,000 jobs added from 37,000.
"Though layoffs continue to be rare, a hesitancy to hire and a reluctance to replace departing workers led to job losses last month," Nela Richardson, ADP's chief economist, said in a press release published Wednesday morning.
To be sure, the ADP report has a spotty track record on predicting the subsequent government jobs report, which investors tend to weigh more heavily. May's soft ADP data ended up differing significantly from the
monthly jobs report figures
that came later in the week.
This week, the government's nonfarm payrolls report will be out on Thursday with economists expecting a healthy 110,000 increase for June, per Dow Jones estimates. Economists are expecting the unemployment rate to tick higher to 4.3% from 4.2%. Some economists could revise down their jobs reports estimates following ADP's data.
Weekly jobless claims data is also due Thursday, with economists penciling in 240,000. This string of labor stats comes during a shortened trading week, with the market closing early on Thursday and remaining dark on Friday in honor of the July Fourth holiday.
Service roles hit hardest
The bulk of job losses came in service roles tied to professional and business services and health and education, according to ADP. Professional/business services notched a decline of 56,000, while health/education saw a net loss of 52,000.
Financial activity roles also contributed to the month's decline with a drop of 14,000 on balance.
But the contraction was capped by payroll expansions in goods-producing roles across industries such as manufacturing and mining. All together, goods-producing positions grew by 32,000 in the month, while payrolls for service roles overall fell by 66,000.
The Midwest and Western U.S. saw the strongest contractions in June, declining by 24,000 and 20,000, respectively. Meanwhile, the Northeast shed 3,000 roles. The Southern U.S. was the sole region tracked by the ADP to see payrolls expand on net in the month, recording an increase of 13,000 positions.
The smallest firms tended to see more job losses in the month than their larger counterparts. In fact, businesses with more than 500 employees saw the biggest payroll growth in the month with an increase of 30,000, per ADP. By comparison, businesses with fewer than 20 employees accounted for 29,000 lost roles on net.
Annual income growth decreased modestly from May for both job stayers and hoppers. The rate of pay increase for those staying in their jobs ticked down to 4.4% from 4.5%, while those getting new roles slid to 6.8% from 7%.
The S&P 500 is up more than 4% for the year, posting a stunning comeback in the second quarter after worries about President
Donald Trump
's tariff fights nearly sent the benchmark into a bear market.
Clarification: The ADP report issued Wednesday referred to June data. That was not clear in an earlier version.

Chatbot Flow Editor
Visual development tool for creating chatbot conversation flows
A GUI tool that opens in your browser. Design, test, and export chatbot conversation flows as JSON.
Quick Start
#
Install as development dependency
npm install --save-dev @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
#
Launch the visual editor
npx @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
Your browser will automatically open with the visual flow editor at
http://localhost:3001
.
Installation & Usage
Method 1: Using npx
npm install --save-dev @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
npx @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
Method 2: Add to your project scripts
Add to your
package.json
{
"scripts"
: {
"design-flows"
:
"
chatbot-flow-editor
"
}
}
Then run
npm run design-flows
Method 3: Global installation
npm install -g @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
chatbot-flow-editor
Usage
Starting the Editor
#
Default (opens on http://localhost:3001)
chatbot-flow-editor
#
Custom port
PORT=4000 chatbot-flow-editor
Available Commands
chatbot-flow-editor start

Start the editor (default)
chatbot-flow-editor
help
#
Show help
chatbot-flow-editor version

Show version

Launch
: Run
npx @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor
Create Nodes
: Click "Add Node" to create conversation points
Edit Content
: Click any node to modify its content and options
Test Flow
: Use the chat preview to simulate user interactions
Export JSON
: Download your flows as structured JSON files
Import Flows
: Load existing JSON flows to continue editing

In your chatbot project directory
npm install --save-dev @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor

Design your conversation flows
npx @enumura/chatbot-flow-editor

Export the flow as JSON

data.title: IntyBASIC: A Basic Compiler for Intellivision
data.author: joemanaco
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Intellivision游戏开发的BASIC编译器——IntyBASIC。作者在开发Intellivision游戏《Space Raid》时，希望简化游戏开发过程，于2013年10月开始开发IntyBASIC，并于2014年1月发布首个版本。IntyBASIC是一个跨平台编译器，可将BASIC源代码转换为CP1610汇编代码，支持Intellivision的视频和声音功能，如SPRITE和SOUND命令。该工具受到了AtariAge社区的欢迎，并促成了多个新游戏和自制游戏的诞生，甚至催生了IntyBASIC编程竞赛。

文章还介绍了IntyBASIC的多个版本更新及其下载途径，建议用户在AtariAge论坛获取最新版本和支持。此外，作者还撰写了两本关于Intellivision游戏编程的书籍，一本针对基础编程，另一本则涵盖更高级技术和实例，如游戏《Oh Mummy!》、《Pumpkin Master》、《Meteor Storm》和《Dungeon Warrior》的源代码和开发技巧。书籍提供了纸质版和电子版购买链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BASIC语言是否是适合初学者的最佳编程语言

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持BASIC作为初学者最佳语言  
  — 论据：BASIC能够激发初学者对编程的热爱  
  — 例子：尽管当今有许多优秀的编程语言，但BASIC在初学编程者中仍然表现出色  
  
• 观点二：对BASIC是否仍是最佳选择存在质疑（隐含观点）  
  — 论据：当前有许多其他优秀的编程语言，可能在某些方面优于BASIC  
  — 例子：提及了当今存在的其他编程语言，暗示可能有更现代的选择适合初学者  

补充讨论：
— 评论中提到了现代编程语言与BASIC的对比，但未具体展开哪些现代语言更适合或为什么。
— 争议焦点在于BASIC是否依然具备相对于现代语言的优势，特别是在激发初学者兴趣方面。

IntyBASIC: a BASIC compiler for Intellivision
Sections:
Downloads
The book
The 2nd book
Useful links
I was working in
Space Raid
for Intellivision when I wondered about possibilities to make easier the
development of games for Intellivision.
There is a full set of tools for emulation (
jzintv
) and
programming in assembler (as1600) created by Joseph Zbiciak (intvnut).
But in every program you need to start almost from zero
and there are few libraries.
The Intellivision console
The Intellivision being created in 1979 just around the same
time BASIC exploded as a general purpose microcomputer language, what would be
more natural than a BASIC compiler? ;)
I started working in October 2013 in my ultrasecret project
and the version 0.1 got published in January 28, 2014 with versions for
Windows, Mac and Linux.
Following the intvnut's toolset style, IntyBASIC is a cross
compiler that takes BASIC source code and translates it to CP1610 assembler
code. You only have to enter this to test your game:
intybasic game.bas game.asm
as1600 game.asm -o game
jzintv game
IntyBASIC includes support for all the Intellivision video
and sound features in form of commands like SPRITE and SOUND,
trying to be close to the hardware but so easy as possible to user.
I've keeping it updated as users and myself find bugs
or request new useful features for the compiler.
It includes also the IntyColor utility for converting BMP
images to the video format used by the Intellivision.
IntyBASIC has been pretty successful in its purpose because
the enthusiast
AtariAge
members community
and it has conducted to an explosion of new games and homebrews in the
Intellivision world and even the
IntyBASIC programming contest
.
Downloads
I suggest you to download the most recent version (v1.4.2)
from the AtariAge forums.
Latest source code of IntyBASIC and IntyColor
, sometimes with new features still not released officially.
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.4.x
(Jan/10/2019).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.2.x
(Aug/08/2015) also check the
IntyBASIC SDK v1.1.1 for Windows
(installer including emulator/assembler).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.1
(Jul/14/2015) also check the
IntyBASIC SDK for Windows
(installer including emulator/assembler).
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v1.0
(Nov/21/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.9
(Oct/10/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.8
(Aug/26/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.7
(Apr/02/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.5-v0.6
(Mar/03/2014)
IntyBASIC cross-compiler v0.1-v0.4
(Jan/27/2014)
The Windows version of IntyBASIC works since XP, but if
your version doesn't have service packs it could need the
Visual C++ 2008 runtime
.
If you're using Mac, you need Mac OS X v10.6 or better. In
case of Linux, any recent version should work.
The user's manual is included inside the ZIP file.
I suggest strongly to register in AtariAge where you can
get help on using IntyBASIC just by reading the
Intellivision Programming
forum or posting your questions.
The book
The success of IntyBASIC inspired me to write a book called "Programming Games for Intellivision".
It follows the learning technique that was so useful for me when starting in the BASIC language: Games published in parts,
required to be typed by hand, and detailed explanation of each part.
The book has 192 pages, and is available both in paperback and hardcover:
Hardcover from
Lulu.com
and
Amazon.com
.
Paperback from
Lulu.com
and
Amazon.com
.
Also available as
ebook from my digital store
.
Check the reviews by
The No Swear Gamer
and a cool hands-on review by
Gray Defender
.
Advanced Game Programming for Intellivision
Inspired by the success of my first book, I went to write another book including more advanced techniques of programming. In particular I wanted to explore the development of games looking more professional both on terms of title screens, gameplay, sound, and music.
The complete source code for Oh Mummy! Pumpkin Master, Meteor Storm, and Dungeon Warrior is included. Each of these games includes a particular technique that I wanted to comment: Oh Mummy! movement of the player on a maze, and how enemies pursue the player. Pumpkin Master, shooters techniques to create tons of bullets without exceeding total sprites. Meteor Storm, techniques for pseudo-3D scaling of sprites, animation of screen zones with multiple images. Dungeon Warrior, techniques for drawing pseudo-3D mazes on screen, including scaling of enemies per depth, and of course algorithms for Role Playing Games.
A full chapter dedicated to the creation of sound effects and converting music sheets to IntyBASIC is included, furthermore tips for converting pictures to Intellivision graphics.
The book has 294 pages, and is available in paperback: (Soon in hardcover)
Paperback from
Lulu.com
and
Amazon.com
.
Also available as
ebook from my digital store
.

data.title: More assorted notes on Liquid Glass
data.author: freediver
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了苹果公司最新的用户界面 redesign，称为“Liquid Glass”，作者对其设计逻辑感到困惑。作者指出，苹果建议导航元素如标签栏和侧边栏浮动在内容层之上，以帮助用户聚焦于底层内容，但这与他们随后建议的“明确区分内容与导航元素”相矛盾。此外，增加空白区域以让内容“呼吸”被认为是不必要的，因为它减少了屏幕上显示的信息量。作者还批评了 redesign 中拉伸开关等变化，认为这些只是为了改变而改变。最后，作者对苹果的“同心设计”和“一致性”等设计指导原则的表述感到不满，认为其用词过于 pretentious 且自相矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS的Liquid Glass设计语言及其相关用户界面（UI）变化的合理性和影响

不同观点：
• [cnrad] 认为Liquid Glass设计牺牲了界面的个性与乐趣，追求极简和空洞的美学，可能不利于用户体验。他希望UI设计能回归更多创意，而不是一味追求空间层次感。
• [prng2021] 质疑苹果为何会批准如此糟糕的UI变化，尤其是在用户反馈不佳的情况下。他怀疑苹果可能在赌“酷炫效果”会掩盖可用性问题。
• [hcarvalhoalves] 提出Apple可能正在为未来的VR设计铺路，通过透明的层级设计来统一UI，以便在虚拟现实中实现内容与控制的灵活布局。
• [jm4] 起初对Liquid Glass有期待，但在使用beta版后感到失望，指出按钮不清晰、低对比度文本和动画卡顿等问题，尽管如此，他仍对未来的改进抱有希望。
• [mglikesbikes] 认为尽管新设计存在可用性问题，但苹果通过这种变化为设备注入了新的生命力，特别是锁屏功能。他指出非技术用户可能不会太在意这些问题，并相信随着时间推移，设计会逐步完善。
• [cedws] 特别不喜欢圆角设计，认为在有限屏幕空间中，这种设计减少了按钮的有效点击区域，增加了视觉噪音。
• [SirMaster] 表示会立即启用“减少透明度”选项，表明对透明效果的不满。

• 尽管存在争议，部分用户仍对未来的改进抱有希望，并认为新设计能为成熟设备注入新活力。

44441279.article_content:
Over the past couple of weeks, I’ve been trying to make sense of Apple’s latest user-interface redesign — Apple calls it
Liquid Glass
— that will affect all their platforms in the next iteration of their respective OS versions. But it’s hard to make sense of it when, after checking Apple’s own guidance, I’m mostly left with the feeling that at Apple they’re making things up as they go.
If you’ve been following me on Mastodon, you’ll be already familiar with a lot of what follows. I just wanted to gather my posts there in a more organic piece here.
Let’s start with a few notes on
Adopting Liquid Glass
, part of the Technology Overviews Apple has made available on their
Developer
site.
In the
Navigation
section, we find this figure:
The text above it says:
Key navigation elements like tab bars and sidebars float in this Liquid Glass layer to help people focus on the underlying content.
Now take a look at the area I’ve highlighted in the image. Why would you want to “focus on the underlying content” here? Tab bars and toolbars still cover the underlying content, and the more transparent/translucent they are, the worse. When something fades to the background, it literally ceases to be in the foreground, so there’s no point in focusing on it. This is like proposing an interface that helps you focus your sight on your peripheral vision.
Below the figure, in the paragraph starting with
Establish a clear navigation hierarchy
, developers are advised to:
Ensure that you clearly separate your content from navigation elements, like tab bars and sidebars, to establish a distinct functional layer above the content layer.
Which is in direct contrast to what you’ve just shown on the image above. First you propose to blur the lines between controls and content, then you advise to “clearly separate your content from navigation elements”. Which is it? If you stop and think, it’s ironic that
Ensure that you clearly separate your content from navigation elements, like tab bars and sidebars, to establish a distinct functional layer above the content layer
is the exact description of what’s happening in the ‘Before’ image!
Moving on, we get to this figure related to the
Extend content beneath sidebars and inspectors
paragraph:
In other words, create the illusion of an image that extends under a sidebar, and while you won’t actually be able to see the part of the image under the sidebar, on the other hand the transparency effect applied to the sidebar will make the text on it less legible overall. A great lose-lose situation, visually, don’t you think? Also, this might be just a matter of personal perception, but to my eyes, the blank area below the image you can see behind the sidebar looks weird, as if there’s something missing.
In
Organisation and layout
we find this:
To give content room to breathe, organizational components like lists, tables, and forms have a larger row height and padding. Sections have an increased corner radius to match the curvature of controls across the system.
Which is largely unnecessary. It reduces the amount of information displayed on screen, and you’ll have to scroll more as a consequence. Look at the Before and After layouts: the Before layout doesn’t need solutions to increase its clarity. You’re just injecting white space everywhere. It’s also ironic that where more space and ‘breathing room’ are actually necessary, the header (“Single Table Row” in the figure) is pushed even nearer to the status bar.
And don’t get me started on those redesigned, stretched-out switches. They’re the essence of ‘change for change’s sake’.
Then I went to have a look at the current
Human Interface Guidelines
and I still can’t get over that introduction:
Let’s start with
Hierarchy
: “Elevate and distinguish the content beneath them”: is this really the role of controls and interface elements? Should content and controls even occupy the same space? Should the lines be blurred between them?
In my opinion, the best way both controls and content can shine is by having each their own space: controls are out of content’s way, letting it shine and helping the user focus on it. And in their own space, controls can be clear, neatly organised, ready to be accessed in order to manipulate the content.
Next,
Harmony
:
Align with the concentric design of the hardware and software […]
No, seriously, how does one
align
in a
concentric
context? Is that a matter of picking a circle, an arc, a shape? All snark aside, this just sounds poorly worded to me. I get what Apple means here: in your app design, you should pick shapes that resemble the contours of the hardware — the shape of a MacBook’s display and bezel, for example — and the typical shapes that you find in the system’s UI. Pretty obvious stuff that’s wrapped in ‘pretentious designer vocabulary’.
Last but not least,
Consistency
:
[…] to maintain a consistent design that continuously adapts […]
The definition of
consistent
is something that is “unchanging in nature, standard,

data.title: Microsoft to Cut 9k Workers in Second Wave of Major Layoffs
data.author: htrp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软大规模裁员的合理性及其背后的商业逻辑

不同观点：
• [idkwhattocallme] 认为微软在盈利丰厚且业务多样化的背景下进行大规模裁员是不合理的。他们指出，公司在过去五年中利润和估值大幅增长，裁员显得无情，且频繁的裁员让人质疑公司对员工的承诺。同时，他们提到工会可能是一个解决方案，以确保员工的工作安全。

• [shadowtree] 指出微软在印度投资30亿美元用于开发者，并大量申请H1B签证，认为这是首席执行官的 predictable behavior（可预见的行为）。这暗示了公司将资源转移至海外，可能与裁员有关。

• [crmd] 分享了其过去的工作经历，提到以前公司对员工的义务被视为最重要的，而现在的公司则通过裁员来提升股价。他们认为这种行为变得常态化，并怀疑与股票回购规则有关。

• [pseudosavant] 通过列举微软的最新季度数据（收入696亿美元，营业收入317亿美元，净利润241亿美元）来质疑裁员的必要性，指出如此高利润下裁员似乎不合理。

• [seatac76] 认为微软的Xbox部门表现不佳，导致需要缩减人员，因为其市场竞争失败和对大公司的收购使其面临困境。

• [jajuuka] 对微软裁员没有明确模式表示困惑，认为裁员没有具体依据，并质疑这种做法对士气的影响。

• [strict9] 指出在关于科技公司大规模裁员的文章中没有提到人工智能（AI），怀疑AI是否已成为裁员和外包的借口。

• [elcritch] 提到微软的生产力软件工具使用体验不佳，认为公司需要这些员工来改善产品。

• [mrtksn] 认为裁员主要集中在销售和市场部门，并提出如果AI工具有效，这些部门应能够通过AI提升市场份额。

• [nyarlathotep_] 担心裁员和外包趋势对本地住房市场的影响，特别是在西雅图这样的城市，高收入年轻人的减少可能影响房市。

• [darthplagius] 提到其在微软的朋友正在开发AI工具以提高员工生产力，但同时公司却在招聘，这显得矛盾。

补充讨论：
• 微软的投资与裁员策略之间的关系，特别是在海外市场和H1B签证上的投入，可能与本地裁员有关。
• 对AI工具在公司内部应用的质疑，以及其是否真的能替代人力。
• 裁员对员工士气和产品质量的潜在影响。
• 裁员趋势对本地经济和房市的潜在影响。

争议焦点：微软在盈利丰厚的情况下进行大规模裁员是否合理，以及这种策略是否更多地与提升股价和资源转移有关。

data.title: The Velvet Sundown are a seemingly AI-generated band with 325k Spotify listeners
data.author: ZeljkoS
data.article_summary: 《The Velvet Sundown》是一个疑似由AI生成的乐队，尽管其在Spotify上拥有超过32.5万月听众，但仅有1,533名追随者，且乐队成员在网络上几乎没有痕迹。其音乐出现在Spotify的Discover Weekly歌单中，并通过多个播放列表获得了大量听众。这些播放列表由一些神秘账户管理，包含了大量该乐队的曲目，尽管乐队与播放列表主题（如越南战争音乐）并无明显关联。此外，该乐队的音乐也被上传至Apple Music、YouTube等平台，且被Deezer识别为可能包含AI生成内容。尽管该乐队引发了广泛讨论，但目前没有确凿证据将其直接与特定AI音乐服务关联。这揭示了AI音乐在流媒体平台上悄然流行，并引发了对AI生成内容如何进入主流音乐的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成音乐的质量、影响以及在平台上的泛滥问题

不同观点：
• **showerst**认为AI生成的音乐质量目前不如人类音乐人，导致听音乐的体验受影响。他指出，尽管他习惯在工作时听音乐，但任何带歌词的音乐都会让他分心，因此他选择听随机的YouTube低保真/ chillout音乐播放列表，然而这些播放列表最近被大量AI生成的音乐充斥。他认为，虽然未来AI音乐可能会达到人类音乐人的水平，但目前质量欠佳，且很难在YouTube上区分AI生成的音乐。

• **cornhole**对AI生成的音乐持较为积极的态度。他提到自己一直在听AI Plankton制作的翻唱歌曲，并认为AI生成的声音效果 surprisingly well（出奇地好），表明他对AI音乐的接受度较高，甚至欣赏某些AI生成的作品。

• **Group_B**认为AI音乐的泛滥是不可避免的趋势，并提出质疑：如果有人 genuinely enjoys（真心喜欢）听AI生成的音乐，那还能称之为slop（劣质音乐）吗？他还关心平台如Spotify如何应对AI音乐的泛滥，以及这种趋势是否只是为了通过广告收入获利。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成音乐的质量和其对用户体验的影响。showerst认为当前的AI音乐质量不高，且难以区分，影响了用户体验；cornhole则认为某些AI生成的音乐质量不错，可以被接受和欣赏；Group_B进一步提出AI音乐是否能被称为劣质音乐的哲学问题，并关注AI音乐对平台经济的潜在影响。

• 讨论还涉及到AI音乐未来的发展趋势，尤其是其质量是否能达到人类音乐人的水平，以及如何在平台上有效管理和筛选AI生成的内容。

44442131.article_content:
Fully AI-generated music is only accounting for
a tiny proportion of streams
on services like Spotify and Deezer at the moment, and there’s an assumption in many parts of the music industry that GenAI music won’t have mainstream appeal.
Which is why it’s so interesting that a band who seem to be AI-generated have more than 325,000 monthly listeners on Spotify. And the longer you spend down the rabbit-hole of The Velvet Sundown, the more interesting it gets.
Credit where it’s due: this story begins on Reddit, with two threads this week calling attention to the band –
here
and
here
– after the music appeared in people’s Discover Weekly playlists. It was then
picked up on TikTok
by musician and author Chris Dalla Riva.
@cdallarivamusic
It was recently uncovered that A.I. generated band is getting hundreds of thousands of streams on Spotify. I break down why this is a problem.
#ai
#aimusic
#spotify
♬ original sound – Chris Dalla Riva
The facts:
The Velvet Sundown have 1,533 followers on Spotify
but 325,388 monthly listeners at the time of writing. “This four-piece band bends time, fusing 1970s psychedelic textures with cinematic alt-pop and dreamy analog soul,” explains their bio.
“Formed by vocalist and mellotron sorcerer Gabe Farrow, guitarist Lennie West, bassist-synth alchemist Milo Rains, and free-spirited percussionist Orion ‘Rio’ Del Mar, the band feels like a hallucination you want to stay lost in.”
The bio includes an approving quote from Billboard – “They sound like the memory of something you never lived, and somehow make it feel real” – which
a Google search suggests has never been published by that trade publication
.
Redditors reckon that the band photo is obviously AI, although in 2025 that could be an aesthetic decision, and have noted the lack of any online footprint for the band or its members.
No results for names as characterful as Milo Rains and Orion Del Mar – assuming Milo isn’t
this cat
– is another red flag. So Music Ally went digging.
First, this isn’t just a Spotify thing: The Velvet Sundown have music available on
Apple Music
,
Amazon Music
,
YouTube
,
Deezer
and other streaming services, although the lack of public metrics there mean we can’t tell how many listeners the band has.
However, the music being on Deezer is helpful, because that service has been developing technology to identify AI-generated music and tag it publicly. “Some tracks on this album may have been created using artificial intelligence,”
is its verdict on both of the band’s albums
.
The music being on YouTube is also helpful, because
each video’s listing reveals
that the music was “provided to YouTube by DistroKid” – meaning that this is the distributor being used by whoever’s uploading the tracks to streaming services. DistroKid’s HyperFollow tool is
also being used for smart-links to The Velvet Sundown’s music
.
So, how is the band reaching so many Spotify listeners? In his TikTok video, Dalla Riva followed the trail from the ‘Discovered On’ section of their profile, which lists the playlists where they are being found by listeners.
We’ve done that too. 25 of the top 30 playlists listed come from just four Spotify accounts:
Extra Music
,
Solitude Collective
,
KULTPOP!
,
In-between
and
Lost Records
. And this is where the rabbit-hole gets ever deeper.
Take Extra Music for example. Its profile has just under 3,000 followers, but its ‘
Vietnam War Music
‘ playlist has 629,311 saves (accounts adding it to their libraries). The 330-song playlist has tracks from a host of Vietnam War-era artists: Creedence Clearwater Revival, the Rolling Stones, Buffalo Springfield, Jimi Hendrix.
Oh, and The Velvet Sundown, whose tracks are nestled at numbers 24, 34, 43, 52, 61, 70, 79, 88, 97, 106, 115, 124, 133, 142, 151, 160, 169, 178, 187, 196, 205, 214, 223, 232, 241 and 250 in its running order. 26 tracks in all – 7.9% of the entire playlist for a band with no obvious ties to the war.
It’s a similar story for Solitude Collective. 2,002 followers but 112,609 saves for its ‘
The OC Soundtrack [All Seasons]
‘ playlist, which includes famous musical moments from the US TV show from the likes of Phantom Planet, Imogen Heap, Jeff Buckley, Oasis… and 22 tracks from The Velvet Sundown.
An impressive 13.3% of the entire playlist. Doubly impressive given that The O.C ran from 2003 to 2007, while both of The Velvet Sundown’s albums to date came out in 2025.
Like we said, it’s a rabbit-hole. A network of playlists with tens or hundreds of thousands of followers, from mysterious curator accounts, stuffed with tracks from a band who don’t appear to exist. And now that band is appearing in people’s Discover Weekly playlists.
(Yes, there is
an account called Velvet Sundown on AI-music service Suno
, but its public tracks’ titles don’t match the ones for the band on streaming services, so it’s not a proven link.)

data.title: Show HN: Spegel, a Terminal Browser That Uses LLMs to Rewrite Webpages
data.author: simedw
data.article_summary: Spegel是一款概念验证的终端浏览器，利用大型语言模型（LLM）处理网页HTML，并以markdown格式在终端显示。用户可以通过自定义提示词调整网页内容展示，满足个性化需求，如简化文本或提取关键步骤。Spegel通过配置文件（~/.spegel.toml）中的提示词处理网页内容，并使用Textual渲染输出。其设计目的是为了去除网页多余信息，专注于用户感兴趣的内容。虽然目前仅支持GET请求且处于早期阶段，但已可通过pip安装并使用。项目源码可在GitHub查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过LLM（大型语言模型）优化网页浏览的方式及其潜在应用和挑战

不同观点：
• **支持与 enthusiasm**：
   - **qsort**：认为该项目很酷，可以作为传统浏览器的替代方案，尤其适用于结合确定性搜索和提示的浏览方式。还建议了多标签功能，但质疑当前最先进模型是否能支持这种工作流。
   - **bubblyworld**：对项目表示赞赏，特别是能去除冗余内容如食谱网站的无关信息，认为这是一个很好的小项目。
   - **mromanuk**：支持LLM作为过滤工具，能绕过SEO优化带来的无效信息，提取有用内容。
   - **ghm2180**：对项目表示兴趣，并建议增加浏览器工具以处理需要身份验证的页面，满足个人用例需求。
   - **gvison**：认为项目比在浏览器中打开网页更节省内存。
   - **ohadron**：认为该项目在提升网页可访问性方面有很大价值。

• **技术实现的质疑与建议**：
   - **leroman**：虽然认为项目有趣，但觉得资源浪费，建议先通过工具将网页转换为markdown以保留语义结构并节省能量。
   - **treyd**：建议使用较不复杂的模型（如基于LSTM的模型）在本地提取所需网页内容，并认为可以轻松生成训练数据。
   - **hambes**：对终端浏览网页的方案表示怀疑，认为该方案未解决主要问题，如JavaScript和动态内容处理。
   - **clbrmbr**：建议增加选项以提取特定内容（如产品评论），提高工具的实用性。
   - **hyperific**：建议结合pandoc工具，先将HTML转换为markdown再由LLM精简内容。

• **潜在问题与风险**：
   - **robbles**：担心LLM在转换数据时可能会出现“幻觉”（即输出内容与输入数据有偏差），导致信息误导。
   
• **扩展应用与未来展望**：
   - **Jotalea**：认为项目资源消耗大，但可以用于旧硬件上的网站适配，同时也可用于广告屏蔽，但效率较低。
   - **__MatrixMan__**：建议增加智能判断功能，避免重复处理同一网页，提升效率。
   - **kelsey98765431**：指出该项目不限于HTML处理，可以扩展到其他格式如PDF、JSON等，核心在于“视图”而非输入格式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于项目的实际效用与资源消耗的平衡，部分人认为项目资源浪费，建议优化；部分人则认为在特定场景下非常有用。
• 技术实现上，存在对LLM模型能力、JavaScript处理、数据准确性等问题的讨论，并提出了多种替代方案或改进建议。
• 项目的潜在应用场景广泛，包括SEO绕过、内容过滤、可访问性提升、旧硬件适配等，但具体实现仍待进一步探索。

44433409.article_content:
Spegel - A Terminal Browser That Uses LLMs to Rewrite Webpages
June 23, 2025
TL;DR Spegel is a proof-of-concept terminal web browser that feeds HTML through an LLM and renders the result as markdown directly in your terminal.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Two weekends ago, after my family had gone to sleep, I found myself unsupervised with a laptop and an itch to build something interesting. A couple of hours later, I had a minimal web browser running in my terminal (no JavaScript, GET requests only) that transformed web content based on my custom prompts.
Then, a few days later, Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro Lite, significantly faster inference speed, suddenly my little weekend hack became a tad more practical.
Personalisation
Adapting content to suit individual needs isn’t a new idea, think about translating books or summarising lengthy articles. However, this used to be slow and expensive. LLMs have changed this dramatically, making these transformations quick and easy.
Spegel ("mirror" in Swedish) lets you explore web content through personalized views using your own prompts. A single page can have multiple views, maybe one simplifying everything down to ELI5 or another highlighting key actions. It's entirely up to you and your prompting skills.
Sometimes you don't want to read through someone's life story just to get to a recipe.
A previous version of this screenshot showed an incorrect recipe on the right. That was due to a bug where large websites got truncated. Thanks to everyone who pointed it out!
That said,
this is a great recipe
Example configuration
[[views]]
id
=
"recipe"
name
=
"Recipe"
hotkey
=
"7"
order
=
"7"
enabled
=
true
auto_load
=
false
description
=
"Get to the point in recipes"
icon
=
"🍳"
prompt
=
"""Parse a recipe and extract only the essential parts.
Format the output like this:
# Ingredients
* 1 tbsp salt
* 400 g beef
# Steps
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C (Gas Mark 6).
2. Wash and chop the carrots.
-----
**Instructions:**
* Use **metric units** (not imperial).
* inches -> cm
* pounds -> kg
* cups -> dl
* Keep the output **clean and minimal** no extra commentary, tips, or nutrition facts.
* Include the servings."""
How it works
The pipeline is straightforward.
Spegel fetches HTML content, processes it through an LLM using prompts stored in a config file (~/.spegel.toml), and outputs markdown rendered via Textual. Prompts and views can be adjusted live during a browsing session.
This was my first experience using Textual for a TUI, and it's been delightful, possibly too delightful, as I found myself adding a few unnecessary interface elements just because it was easy.
One gotcha was ensuring only completed lines (ending in newline characters) were streamed; otherwise, the markdown renderer would parse incomplete markdown and fail to recover formatting

Other terminal browsers
There are a lot of great terminal browsers out there, Lynx and Links2 are close to my heart. There are also modern attempts like Browsh that can even render graphs using half-block Unicode characters (▄█).
Spegel isn’t meant to replace these, it’s more of an exploration or proof-of-concept. It currently doesn't support POST requests (though I have some ideas on handling
<form>
elements by creating on-the-fly UIs).
But most modern websites aren’t designed with terminal browsing in mind. They rely on CSS and JS, making them cumbersome in small terminal windows, full of clutter and noise. Spegel tries to clear away distractions, providing content tailored more closely to your needs.
Try it
Spegel is still in the early stages, so expect some rough edges, but it’s usable and kind of fun to play with.
Install it via pip:

install

Then just run it with a URL:

data.title: The Chapel Programming Language
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: Chapel编程语言是一款专注于高效并行计算的语言，适用于从个人电脑到超级计算机的各种规模。它具备生产力高、语法简洁、易读且不牺牲速度和表达能力等特点。Chapel内置支持多种并行计算模式，无需在抽象层次和低级控制之间妥协，并且能够直接在GPU上运行而无需复杂的API。文章展示了多个示例，包括分布式"Hello World"、并行文件I/O、1D热传导模拟和GPU核函数操作。Chapel已被多个项目采用，如CHAMPS多物理场模拟、Arkouda大数据分析和Coral Reef生物多样性分析，证明了其在实际生产环境中的高效性和易用性。用户反馈强调了其代码可读性和易维护性，使其特别适合教育和研究环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论中主要讨论了一种并行计算 focused 的编程语言的发展及其创新潜力，同时涉及其在高效能计算（HPC）中的应用和性能表现。

不同观点：
• [aus10d] 认为该语言聚焦于并行计算是一个重要的发展方向，并提出未来其他语言如何在这一主题上继续创新的疑问。他强调了并行计算在未来技术发展中的关键性。

• [pjmlp] 表示对该语言的长期关注，指出其在一些高性能计算中心（HPC centers）中开始流行。他还提到该语言采用了一种类似仿射类型系统（affine type system）来进行资源管理，并与其他语言进行了比较，认为该语言在生产力方面表现突出，不像Rust那么 rigid。

• [Qem] 提供了该语言在浮点基准测试中的优异表现的具体例子，引用了John Walker的网站数据，以此说明该语言在实际计算性能上的优势。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了该语言与Rust在资源管理和类型系统方面的比较，指出了两者在灵活性和生产力上的差异，这是潜在的争议点。

• 评论中也提到了具体的技术特性，如仿射类型系统在资源管理中的应用，显示了技术社区对语言设计细节的关注。

• 最后，通过引用实际的基准测试数据，[Qem] 为该语言的性能优势提供了实证支持，这在讨论中增加了技术可信度。

Try Chapel
Get Chapel
Learn Chapel
Productive
Concise and readable without compromising speed or expressive power. Consistent concepts for parallel computing make it easier to learn.
Parallel
Built from the ground up to implement parallel algorithms at your desired level of abstraction. No need to trade low-level control for convenience.
Fast
Chapel is a compiled language, generating efficient machine code that meets or beats the performance of other languages.
Scalable
Chapel enables application performance at any scale, from laptops to clusters, the cloud, and the largest supercomputers in the world.
GPU-Enabled
Chapel supports vendor-neutral GPU programming with the same language features used for distributed execution. No boilerplate. No cryptic APIs.
Open
Entirely open-source using the Apache 2.0 license. Built by a great community of developers. Join us!
Users Love It
“
The use of Chapel worked as intended: the code maintenance is very much reduced, and its readability is astonishing. This enables undergraduate students to contribute to its development, something almost impossible to think of when using very complex software.
”
- Éric Laurendeau, Professor, Polytechnique Montréal
“
A lot of the nitty gritty is hidden from you until you need to know it. ... It feels like the complexity grows as you get more comfortable -- rather than being hit with everything at once.
”
- Tess Hayes, Developer, Bytoa
Chapel in Production
CHAMPS
World-class multiphysics simulation
Written by students and post-docs in Eric Laurendeau's lab at Polytechnique Montreal. Outperformed its C/OpenMP predecessor using far fewer lines of code. Dramatically accelerated the progress of grad students while also supporting contributions from undergrads for the first time.
Learn More
Arkouda
Interactive data science at massive scale
Familiar Python/Jupyter client interface, powered by a Chapel server that scales to compute and memory resources beyond any comparable tool. Interactively work with dozens of TBs of data.
Learn More
Coral Reef Biodiversity Analysis
Processing oceans of data
The Coral Reef Alliance uses Chapel to analyze satellite imagery of the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, providing biodiversity measurements 5 orders of magnitude faster than the previous solution.
Learn More
ChOp
Exact optimization algorithms at scale
Chapel-based Optimization (ChOp) solves combinatorial optimization problems. It leverages CPU-GPU heterogeneity with high productivity and parallel performance.
Learn More
ChplUltra
Ultralight dark matter simulation
Simulates the astrophysical dynamics of ultra-light dark matter using Chapel's productivity features to compute distributed F

data.title: The Evasive Evitability of Enshittification
data.author: trulyrandom
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了软件公司常面临的“劣化”问题，即产品在初期表现出色，但随着市场垄断的形成，公司为了短期收益开始降低产品质量。这种现象被称为“enshittification”，由Corey Doctorow提出。文章作者Avery认为，产品劣化并非成功的必然结果，而是源于公司对未来发展的恐惧和错误决策。成功的公司通常依赖于用户喜爱的正反馈循环，但这一循环十分脆弱，一旦公司改变战略，可能会破坏这种循环，导致产品质量下降。作者强调，控制权的变更和市场饱和是产品劣化的两大外部诱因。Tailscale承诺不会走上这条道路，并会坚守其核心价值和方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何防止软件或服务的“恶化”（enshittification）以及维持长期生存的策略

不同观点：
• ksynwa认为文章中提出的策略过于笼统和模糊，仅能得出短期内不会达到市场饱和，因此恶化不是迫在眉睫的威胁。同时对引用Google的例子感到讽刺，但仍希望作为免费用户能继续使用服务，因其对他帮助很大。

• armchairhacker指出开源是一种防御手段，但依赖竞争的防御方式可能导致另一种失败模式，即由于缺乏资源而导致的放弃或停滞。当资金耗尽时，恶化或放弃是不可避免的，除非有其他可行的方式获取资金。

• weinzierl认为文章中提到的“防御恶化”的策略不够具体，并提出可以借鉴那些数十年来避免了恶化的软件。这些软件通常具有以下特点：1. 采用copyleft许可证，2. 没有版权转让或贡献者许可协议（CLA），3. 拥有足够大且多样化的贡献者群体以使重新许可 practically impossible。此外，由501(c)(3)组织管理也是一个良好指标。

• _spduchamp质疑是否有具体的公司或产品能够避免恶化，并请求举例说明。

• juped以讽刺的口吻表示，Tailscale可能通过一个糟糕的、自嘲的名字（"tailscale"）来避免恶化，因为这会让风险投资公司失去兴趣。同时对一个实用产品还需要筹集更多资金表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于文章提出的策略是否有效和具体。
• weinzierl提供了基于开源软件历史的具体防御措施，并指出某些许可证和治理结构的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到对具体例子的需求以及对公司筹集资金动机的怀疑。

44443975.article_content:
Blog
|
insights
July 02, 2025
The evasive evitability of enshittification
This post was originally published on Avery’s personal blog as his perspective on a topic that affects nearly every software company. But because it so closely reflects the philosophy we share across the leadership and team at Tailscale — and because it captures the approach we are committed to maintaining — we’re reposting it here as an official statement of our company values and direction.
Tailscale recently
announced
our Series C fundraise. We were grateful for all the community support, but the Internet also raised a few of its collective eyebrows, wondering whether this meant the dreaded “enshittification” was coming next.
That word describes a very real pattern we’ve all seen before: products start great, grow fast, and then slowly become worse as the people running them trade user love for short-term revenue.
It’s a topic I find genuinely fascinating, and I've seen the downward spiral firsthand at companies I once admired. So I want to talk about why this happens, and more importantly, why it won't happen to us. That's big talk, I know. But it's a promise I'm happy for people to hold us to.
What is enshittification?
The term "enshittification" was first popularized in a
blog post by Corey Doctorow
, who put a catchy name to an effect we've all experienced. Software starts off good, then goes bad. How? Why?
Enshittification proposes not just a name, but a mechanism. First, a product is well loved and gains in popularity, market share, and revenue. In fact, it gets so popular that it starts to defeat competitors. Eventually, it's the primary product in the space: a monopoly, or as close as you can get. And then, suddenly, the owners, who are Capitalists, have their evil nature finally revealed and they exploit that monopoly to raise prices and make the product worse, so the captive customers all have to pay more. Quality doesn't matter anymore, only exploitation.
I agree with most of that thesis. I think Doctorow has that mechanism
mostly
right. But, there's one thing that doesn't add up for me:
Enshittification is not a success mechanism.
I can't think of any examples of companies that, in real life, enshittified because they were
successful
. What I've seen is companies that made their product worse because they were… scared.
A company that's growing fast can afford to be optimistic. They create a positive feedback loop: more user love, more word of mouth, more users, more money, more product improvements, more user love, and so on. Everyone in the company can align around that positive feedback loop. It's a beautiful thing. It's also fragile: miss a step and it flattens out and soon it's a downward spiral instead of an upward one.
So, if I were, hypothetically, running a company, I think I would be pretty hesitant to deliberately sacrifice a step from that positive feedback loop, the loop I and the whole company spent so much time and energy building, to see if I can grow faster. User love? Nah, I'm sure we'll be fine, look how much money and how many users we have! Time to switch strategies!
Why would I do that? Whenever you switch strategies, there has to be a threshold moment, when something fundamental changes.
Threshold moments and control
In
Saint John, New Brunswick, there's a river
that flows one direction at high tide, and the other way at low tide. Four times a day, gravity equalizes, then crosses a threshold to gently start pulling the other way, then accelerates. What doesn't happen is a rapidly flowing river in one direction "suddenly" shifts to rapidly flowing the other way. You can see the threshold coming. It's predictable.
In my experience, for a company or a product, there are two kinds of thresholds like this, that when crossed, create a flow change.
The first one is control: if the visionaries in charge lose control, chances are their replacements won't "get it."
The new people didn't build the underlying feedback loop, and so they don't realize how fragile it is. There are lots of reasons for a change in control; financial mismanagement, boards of directors, hostile takeovers.
The worst one is temptation. Being a founder is, well, it actually sucks. It's oddly like being repeatedly punched in the face. When I look back at my career, I guess I'm surprised by how few times per day it feels like I was punched in the face. But, the constant face punching gets to you after a while. Once you've established a great product, and amazing customer love, and lots of money, and an upward spiral, isn't your creation strong enough yet? Can't you step back and let the professionals just run it, confident that they won't kill the golden goose?
Empirically, mostly no, you can't. Actually the success rate of control changes, for well loved products, is abysmal.
The saturation trap
The second trigger of a flow change is comes from outside: saturation. Every successful product, at some point, reaches approximately all the us

data.title: Microsoft to lay off as many as 9k employees in latest round
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软（MSFT）的裁员原因及其影响，特别是与人工智能（GenAI）和股东利益的关系。

不同观点：
• AbbeFaria：作为员工和股东，AbbeFaria认为裁员是有道理的，因为公司内有些工程团队对业务贡献不大。同时，他对裁员的原因感到困惑，怀疑是否是由大股东驱动，或者是为了在生成式人工智能（GenAI）获得收入前节省资金（如GPU成本）。

• nashashmi：nashashmi认为这些裁员不是基于实际技术需求，而是“理论上”的裁员。公司文化倾向于根据需求招聘和裁员，而不是根据员工是否仍然必要。他还提到新任CEO通常会进行一些调整以观察结果，类似于“摇树”策略。

• TurkishPoptart：TurkishPoptart声称被裁员工将由持H1-B签证的AI操作人员取代，暗示外籍劳工可能填补被裁岗位。

• 1970-01-01：这位评论者认为，尽管目前AI还不能完全取代所有被裁员工，但当前情况显示出一种泡沫破裂的迹象。

• fossa1：fossa1指出，尽管公司声称AI将“增强”员工能力，但实际情况似乎是AI正在将员工挤出工作岗位。与此同时，微软的股票接近历史新高，显示出股东是裁员的受益者，而员工则是受害者。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：裁员是基于实际业务需求还是公司文化和领导层的调整策略。AbbeFaria和nashashmi对此有不同看法。
